facts.statement: W-65 reports Goku felling a tree with one punch and carrying it home. The local episode-1 captions give the falling-tree sound and subsequent conversation, not the punch or tree size. A selected fan-gallery still (W-127; cut unverified) shows him poised to strike a tree, not the complete action. An earlier draft claimed it was the biggest on that side; the current selected chapter does not. The punch and Goshin’s accompanying woodpile work are staged in the unaccepted chapter.

facts.previous_statement_before_episode1_still: W-65 reports that Goku fells a tree with one punch and carries it home. The local episode-1 captions give the falling-tree sound and subsequent conversation (05:13–05:52), not the punch or tree size. facts.statement: Episode-1 captions have Chi-Chi call Gohan in for the meal, Goku return and offer to find him, and Chi-Chi say he probably has not gone far (04:37–05:55). The intervening line that they must eat and depart because Roshi and the others are waiting is not speaker-labelled in the SRT. W-65 attributes it to Chi-Chi; the user-authorized Chapter One revision follows that secondary attribution. The captions do not establish how he travels.

facts.statement: In the local episode-2 captions Raditz names Planet Vegeta as Goku's birthplace at 17:01, then later claims that a giant meteor destroyed it, that his and Goku's parents died, and that only four Saiyans including Goku remain (20:29–21:05). These are his limited claims, not final history. In episode 49 Dodoria tells Vegeta Freeza destroyed the planet (23:46–23:53). Much later in the source, Freeza speaks to the Namek group about attacking Planet Vegeta, and Krillin privately realizes Freeza destroyed the Saiyan planet (77, 23:27–23:51; repeated in 78). In episode 86, 20:14–21:22, the dying Vegeta tells Goku that Freeza destroyed Planet Vegeta and killed their fathers, after which Goku responds as an Earth-raised Saiyan (22:29–24:35). In episode 90, 11:05–11:25, Freeza speaks the name Bardock among past opponents; this passage does not itself identify that name to Goku as his father. In the episode-92 captions, subjective speech attributed to Vegeta refers to “your father Bardock” (11:24–12:53); a secondary rewatch calls it a vision. The text alone does not establish its visual framing or how Goku knows the name. Episode 104 retrospectively has Nappa tell Vegeta and Raditz that Freeza caused the destruction, with Vegeta saying he already knew (15:42–17:20); episode 49 instead has Vegeta say he had not known while being used since childhood (24:24–24:32). The tension is unresolved, not an established early handoff (C269). A later official manga-based profile separately reports the broad cause (W-91). The revelation is not shown reaching the early Earth family or Goku at the current branch frontier; do not transfer any later source character's knowledge without a branch-specific handoff.

facts.statement: Half-Saiyan, with the two lineages fused. The existing working design gives him Gohan’s height and a slightly heavier build through the shoulders. The original percentage is an appearance comparison, not a genetics formula or a required line of prose. No additional eye colour or fixed costume is established. The earlier R-22 wording wrongly treated the physical design as retired; habits and personality complement it, not replace it.

facts.statement: The exceptional innate Adaptation Talent is supernatural, non-sentient and acts on Goshin’s whole being. It supports cumulative development of body, whole Saiyan–Earthling hybrid inheritance, recovery, senses, instincts, ki, fighting, skills and compatible new abilities; rapid learning and retention are expressions, not its entire scope. The Talent grows with its holder. Training, experience, life, combat and recovery can all contribute; in-fight growth can be rapid and substantial. No fixed growth rate, free exact reading or automatic immunity is assigned. The author confirms that the Talent, the evolving hybrid bloodline and the rest of Goshin can develop and interact as one broader whole, alongside life, experience and other influences; the listed aspects are examples, not an exhaustive limit (`O244`).
facts.source_class: OC — author ruling

facts.statement: Super Saiyan 1, 2 and 3 are **perfected** and therefore not forms he enters: they are internal, instant, and never announced. No hair beat, no lightning, no counting. The power is simply present.

The form remains future and unshown. Chapter Six's 1,500 is a separate ordinary-ki anger surge, not an early transformation. Do not make all of Goshin's anger silent or emotionless.

facts.statement: Super Saiyan 4 is his planned physical apex, earned on the ape road with his tail kept and a future Golden Ape route, not the Daima gift. The earlier wording that the ape must cost him fear is superseded by the later author direction: Goshin is aware and in control from his first Great Ape, without mandatory fear of the form or a required loss-of-control arc. His Saiyan traits and ape power develop with him; the first trigger is staged in the unaccepted Chapter 26 candidate when Goshin deliberately looks at Vegeta's artificial moon; later development and SS4 scenes remain unwritten. OPEN-3 remains closed: the tail is kept.
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: Super Saiyan Blue is excluded for Goshin by the serial’s authored structural rationale: his perfected first form is internal and his later adapted godly base is permanent. This is a character-specific creative rule, not evidence that all canonical Blue users are mortal borrowers of god ki. His later god rungs remain separately authored (O038).
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: After the crossing, **Super Saiyan God is not a form he takes: it is his base** — what he is at rest. The physical apex (Super Saiyan 4) is earned first, the crossing comes late, and Super Saiyan 4 over a divine base is the last rung.
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: **God 1, God 2 and God 3 are conversions, not inventions.** His base is Super Saiyan God, so when he reaches for Super Saiyan 1, 2 or 3 the divine base is folded into the reaching and the divine rung is what arrives — same degree, same three gears, different substrate. **Each rung leaks**, so the climb makes him louder. God 1/2/3 is *like* Super Saiyan 1/2/3 the way a translation is like the page it came from. This is an authored future presentation for Goshin, not an independently established general canon law.
facts.source_class: authored (O)

The former record additionally interpreted it through calm instinct and damage-fed cold rage, but the direct user provenance of those specific emotional mechanics is unverified. It is future and unwritten; do not impose an automatic mood switch or limit present emotion.

facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: **The ultimate: Super Saiyan God worn inside the Super Saiyan 4 body.** The fusion of his two roads, in canon's Ultra class and not canon's (UI and UE stay other people's). Its character is the two states he already owns: **instinct when he is calm** (the body answers before he decides), **ego when he is not** (cold rage feeding on damage). **Leakage stops — fur is a vessel — so the crown is quieter than the rung below it**, and slower to arrive, because the body must accept it first.

facts.statement: The Talent retains what has genuinely been learned or adapted; holding back, fatigue, injury or distraction can temporarily impair use or lower a reading without forgetting the skill. Preserve the separately ruled future divine promotion and conversions (STATUS §§12–14).
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: The secondary Super Saiyan God wiki describes the form as cool-headed and beneficial to ki control, while also acknowledging that a user can become angry. This is not evidence that godhood removes all emotions, temperament or identity, nor a universal rule for every version. Goshin's retention of emotional capacity is a separate future authored decision (O043); a calm scene is not forbidden.
facts.source_class: wiki-form-page
facts.previous_statement_before_complete_canon: Canon describes Super Saiyan God as **cooling its user** — a calm mind, steadier ki control, described as one of the form's benefits. One encyclopaedic group (C117's source).

facts.statement: **The Talent itself becomes divine and works on everything.** After the crossing his ki, his forms, his techniques and anything he learns afterwards run on **divine qi** — the substrate is what he learns on, so nothing he acquires is ever ordinary again.
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: The planned divine promotion is not to erase Goshin's identity, attachments or capacity for emotion. The earlier assistant-authored instruction to cut any scene where he is serene or distant is an unsupported absolute: he can be calm, sad, playful, angry or distant for contextual reasons. The promotion is future and unshown.
facts.source: earlier STATUS future-promotion record and 3 November emotional-character correction
facts.source_class: future project direction with assistant-added emotional absolute withdrawn
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: **Godhood takes nothing from him.** Canon's form cools a Saiyan (C119); his promotion does not, because the retention law removes nothing (O041). He keeps his temper, appetite, jokes, grudges, grief, mistakes and attachments. **Any scene where godhood makes him serene or distant is a scene to cut.**

facts.statement: **His children are born divine, not mortal.** The line does not begin at a ritual; it begins at him. Ruled; the children themselves are unwritten (OPEN-11).
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: At four and through the Z-era arcs Goshin is mortal and uses ordinary ki, flight and techniques; no early golden transformation, god ki or divine promotion. Mortal means not divine, not an ordinary-human body or ordinary rate of growth. Natural Saiyan Great Ape biology is not prohibited by this era rule, and in unaccepted Chapter 26 Goshin deliberately enters his first Great Ape, aware and controlled; no golden or divine transformation is implied.
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.topic: ep8 the ape and the moon
facts.statement: In the local episode-8 captions, 19:54–23:55, Gohan says he is looking at a full moon for the first time; heartbeat and roars follow. Piccolo's flashback repeats Raditz's full-moon words, though the local episode-2 captions put that exchange at Kame House when Piccolo was absent. Piccolo links the change to moon and tail, says he blew away the moon, considers removing the tail and prepares clothes and a sword. In episode 9, 05:18, Gohan finds the tail absent; in episode 18, 09:14, Piccolo says he pulled it out six months earlier. Those words do not establish complete silent transformation or removal choreography.

facts.statement: In episode 7, 07:50–10:16, Kami tells Popo that Piccolo has changed: Raditz's soul reached the afterlife, whereas those killed by demons had previously wandered without rest. Kami feels his own life and Piccolo's linked life have about a year left, but does not know whether the Saiyans will kill Piccolo or Kami's own life will end of age. He predicts the Dragon Balls can be used once more. The timing, cause and last use are his expressed expectation, not an unconditional guarantee.

facts.statement: A Saiyan's tail can be a gripping weakness (ep. 3); Raditz says an owner can cut off his own tail (ep. 5, 08:53), while Vegeta says he and Nappa trained past the weakness (ep. 27, 07:48). Gohan's tail regrows in episodes 18 and 34. In episode 42 the unlabelled caption says a tail could not be regenerated; the following caption labels Vegeta as saying it will grow back (24:52–24:57). In the episode-43 recap the doctor is labelled immediately before the repeated unlabelled tail statement, providing additional contextual support for the doctor's attribution (03:37–03:49); W-93's secondary guide identifies Vegeta's tail, not Gohan's. Neither caption line is individually speaker-tagged, and neither establishes a universal regrowth rule. Relevant Great Ape triggers include natural or artificial Blutz-wave sources (C148).

facts.statement: Chi-Chi values Gohan's education (ep. 2 and ep. 107), but this is not her whole character: in episode 65 she urgently tries to go to the endangered Gohan using Brief's second ship (C250). In ep. 200, 16:44–16:54, Gohan explicitly says he COMMUTES FROM HOME to his city school; the former claim that he moved to Satan City was wrong. The selected family's circumstances differ. A separate official manga-based feature describes her advancing through the 23rd tournament preliminaries, fighting Goku and impressing Roshi with her combat skill (W-106); it is not a complete pre-Z manga or anime review. Separately, Toei's original-Dragon-Ball episode-137 synopsis describes her fighting Goku at the tournament and their subsequent acceptance of the old marriage promise; its episode-151 synopsis says she finds the fan while helping an older woman. These are short TV descriptions of initiative and shared history, not complete scene viewing or a demand that the branch repeat the adventure (W-113). In original-Z episode 109 she is angry that Gohan left without permission before the mist changes the family's behavior; Krillin's joke that she is the strongest woman in the universe is not an objective power reading. In episode 117 she softens at Turtle's thanks and attends his birthday gathering. These particular TV moments neither require the divergent family to repeat the conflict nor reduce her to it (W-30 W-114).

facts.statement: The local original-Z captions depict Freeza's grievous injury to the still-living Piccolo and killing of Krillin, followed by Goku's first Super Saiyan transformation (95, 17:52–24:23; 96 recap and 06:11–09:31). Goku initially fears losing his reason and orders Gohan to take Piccolo away; he later still makes deliberate protective, competitive and merciful choices (C268). Toei identifies the transformation in its episode-95 synopsis, and an official Krillin feature independently associates Krillin's death with it (W-110 W-111). Goshin's first eventual Great Ape is separately authored as aware and controlled.

facts.statement: A fight is clear in geography, participants, actions, stakes and consequences. Flight, named techniques, multiple supernatural actions and sourced or authored readings are allowed. Damage follows feats, attack, aim and conditions, not a fixed formula (WRITING §§11,16).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: Write supernatural action directly and coherently: cause, movement, effect, consequence. Do not compare it to ordinary furniture, flag it as impossible or report what could not be seen. Multiple supernatural actions and visible ordinary ki are allowed; no early god ki (WRITING §12).
facts.source: author ruling — fights and the supernatural are the weakest writing
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: CRAFT.md has three authored specimens: controlled spar, hillside blast and flight/technique practice. They are exercises, not canonical beats.

facts.statement: **Once a character is named on the page, the narration calls them by that name.** No epithets for named characters — not 'the taller boy', not 'the small one', not 'the demon', not 'the woman with blue hair'. **Three legal exceptions only:** before the name is known (once), for a character who is never named (declared as furniture), and inside dialogue. **Gated by `check_names`.**
facts.source: author ruling — epithets read as withholding
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.topic: craft — the crib, and the clarity law
facts.statement: **A fight must be followable in one pass** (WRITING §11): establish where the participants are, who acts, cause, contact and what changes. Use a name where a pronoun would be ambiguous; connected actions may share a sentence if the sequence remains clear (O048). Every craft specimen carries a plain-words crib first. The former one-action-per-sentence absolute is withdrawn.
facts.source: author ruling — the fight could not be followed
facts.source_class: authored (O)
facts.previous_statement_before_complete_canon: **A fight must be followable in one pass** (`WRITING §11 law 0`): every paragraph answers *where are they · who is acting · what changed*. **One action per sentence; no pronoun with two possible owners.** Effect-only prose is a mood, not a sequence. **Every specimen carries a plain-words crib first** — numbered, adjective-free — because if the crib is unclear the prose is broken, not the reader.

facts.topic: craft — no riddles in invented material
facts.statement: Invented material must be plain and understandable without prior scenes. Characters do not speak in aphorisms or announce facts already shown: the authority orders and the learner acts. Context and action make the stake clear; every craft specimen begins with WHAT THIS IS and a plain-words crib.
facts.source: author ruling — the invented prose reads as a riddle
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.statement: **The impossible runs on flow** (WRITING §15): show cause, movement, effect and consequence. Avoid telling the reader the action could not be seen or interrupting to declare it strange; do not reduce supernatural effects to comparisons with ordinary furniture. Do not have a character redundantly announce an already-visible fact merely to supply a verdict; useful in-context speech is not categorically prohibited (WRITING §14).
facts.source: author ruling — the supernatural comparisons and the announcements read wrong
facts.source_class: authored (O)
facts.previous_statement_before_complete_canon: **The impossible runs on flow** (`WRITING §15`). **Never tell the reader they could not see it** — *no 'nobody saw', no 'blink of an eye'*; write the displacement and let the ground report it. **Never compare the impossible to something ordinary** — no doors, pages, bowls, fists. **Never stop to say it is strange** — the reader knows. Shape: **cause you can point at → event → consequence left in the world**, no gaps. **And a character may not announce what the scene already shows:** no *'he has a tail'* — let the one with authority give the order and the boy act.

facts.statement: A fight declares its participants, condition, relevant demonstrated capabilities, attack and environment. Damage follows the scene and feats, not a numerical battle-power conversion. Bodies are not categorically small-damage and large feats need not always require a long charge (WRITING §16).
facts.source: author ruling — the fight's scale was false
facts.source_class: authored (O)

facts.topic: the numbers do not scale to damage

Ep. 8 dialogue says Piccolo blew away the moon; ep. 22 dialogue reports East City gone following Nappa’s greeting. Piccolo’s 408 and Nappa’s guidebook 4,000 are not contemporaneous readings of those particular attacks. Method, scale, aim, condition and context matter.

Raditz catches Goshin's torn sleeve; Goshin hooks his ankle and pushes against the cracked armour with rising ki, sending Raditz off balance, then tears free and clears the firing line. Piccolo fires his 1,480 second shot while Raditz is falling and unable to dodge in time. The beam pierces Raditz; its spiral grazes Goku's arm. Goku survives, badly hurt. Gohan's frightened release breaks the cliff; Goshin intervenes and catches him before impact. Gohan warns the people at the aircraft, asserts his wish to be a scholar and refuses Piccolo. Piccolo leaves without either child; the coercive assault is not consent or a new friendship.

Goshin opens his hand and catches Gohan with ki, bending his path away from the rock, then flies after him. After Gohan’s burst, Goshin uses ki against a falling slab and catches Gohan in flight. The older root draft explicitly described copied hand movement and a later gauze-roll lift; those specific beats are not shown in the selected chapter. Do not erase the selected ki feat or assert a maximum or a precisely stated acquisition mechanism.

His first limited non-contact pull shifts Gohan; another changes the thrown child's course, and Goshin flies to catch him. Later he repeats the gesture to lift and catch a small roll of gauze. The technique is learned and retained in this authored scene but is not demonstrated at unlimited range or full mastery; no hidden biological regeneration is copied. The user later clarified that instinctive copying in an emergency remains allowed under the mastery-first training priority (O104).

facts.previous_branch_statement: Goshin fires the Kamehameha learned from Goku in Chapter Five to divert falling stone away from the aircraft toward an empty crater wall. The unmeasured wave wavers and scars unoccupied rock; his bandage is singed and his burned hand hurts. The prior 1,450 first-wave scan and later 1,500 surge are separate snapshots, not a new reading, a cap or a damage equation.

facts.topic: chapter seven — Kami asks about King Kai
facts.statement: In selected unaccepted Chapter Seven, Kami independently asks Yemma for help against the approaching Saiyans and whether King Kai might see living Goku. Yemma reports judging and restraining dead Raditz, says King Kai decides whom he helps and agrees to ask, without promising an answer or granting passage. He describes the road's traditional length, but no guide shows Kami its entrance in this selected scene. Kami and Popo discuss Raditz's arrival in the afterlife in Chapter Eight without declaring Piccolo reformed. Goku is alive, not in Otherworld, and has not started Snake Way. A guide's road tour and the explicit later-fit-request conditions belonged to an older treatment.
facts.source: authored Chapter Seven, adapting C114 C128 C170
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and consequence
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: Kami independently asks Yemma for help against the coming Saiyans. Yemma reports restraining and sending dead Raditz to Hell; the question about Piccolo's victim is brought forward from the baseline's later discussion without declaring Piccolo reformed. Kami asks about living Goku seeking King Kai's training. Yemma does not grant permission and asks for a later request when Goku is willing and fit; a guide shows Kami the road's entrance only. Goku is not in Otherworld and has not started Snake Way.

facts.statement: Chapter Three shows the single Ox-King visit, an unanswered Kame House call, and a call to the exchange. Selected Chapter Seven continues that visit with a later, separate call answered by Turtle; Chi-Chi and her father leave in his truck. Do not conflate the two Kame House calls or attribute the later telling to Roshi. Chapter Three's external-camera ruling is scoped to that chapter.
facts.source: authored Chapter Seven overlap with revised Chapter Three and C066 C111
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and consequence
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Chapter Seven reuses revised Chapter Three’s single Ox-King visit and unanswered Kame House call, expanding Chi-Chi’s worry in that overlap. After her exchange call, Roshi calls promptly from Kame House and she and her father set out in his truck to meet Bulma. The approved Chapter Three revision removes the earlier 4 December date, rigid countdown and incompatible grandfather-at-home overnight ending; the earlier body is preserved historically.

facts.statement: The selected Chapter Seven scouter remains unpowered, with its cell separate in Bulma's pocket. The damaged aircraft is at the river clearing, not Kame House; Bulma intends to study the device but has not decoded it or proved that it cannot transmit. The Dragon Radar remains in Roshi's medical case.
facts.source: authored Chapter Seven, continuing O093 and adapting C107
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and consequence
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: The scouter and removed cell stay wrapped separately in Bulma's medical case. She discusses examining the transmitter and potentially locating Yamcha and Tien, but has not decoded the language, established a safe operating procedure or powered the device on. Its original retrieval occurred in Chapter Six and is not repeated. The case is at Kame House when Bulma leaves to meet Chi-Chi and the Ox-King; whether both fit in the aircraft has not been established. This describes the end of Chapter Seven; Chapter Eight subsequently shows both Chi-Chi and Ox-King fitting in the aircraft (O106).

facts.topic: Korin Tower and restorative Senzu — pre-Z background
facts.statement: Official manga-based W-53 identifies Karin as the tower's resident and associates Yajirobe with bean delivery. Secondary W-54 says Korin grows Senzu, describes their restoration of injuries and energy, and reports Yajirobe giving Goku one after the 23rd tournament. No consulted source establishes Korin's exact stock or Yajirobe's presence at the altered episode-6 moment; no complete DB footage was checked.

facts.source_class: official manga-based feature and secondary franchise overview; DB video unverified

W-55 previously reported the same broad point as a secondary account; the independence of its two articles remains uncertain. Neither is a complete episode viewing, and no particular long-distance speed, endurance or travel time for the altered trip to Korin follows.

facts.topic: chapter seven — Krillin, Korin and three Senzu
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Seven Korin gives Krillin three Senzu and Krillin flies toward the boys. In Chapter Eight Krillin reaches the riverbank: Goku eats one whole bean and Gohan later eats one, fully restoring both. Goshin suggests Gohan take one, chooses medical care for himself and wants the last kept for an emergency; Krillin keeps it. He also asks to see where Korin grows the beans. The choice does not establish an unbreakable refusal of unseen food; no new scan or automatic Zenkai is shown.
facts.source: authored corrected Chapter Seven using pre-Z resources described in C172 C173
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and consequence
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: In the corrected Chapter Seven draft, Krillin flies from the crater to Korin Tower while the others prepare to return to Kame House. Korin has three Senzu to spare, and Yajirobe is present; their exact contemporaneous stock and presence are authored, not episode-6 facts. Krillin brings them to Kame House. Goku and Gohan each eat one and their battle injuries heal completely; their strength is fully restored, with no residual battle pain or fatigue. The user explicitly corrected the full-restoration rule. Goshin declines the third because he did not watch it being made (STATUS §5); his head and hand remain sore, the bean is kept, and the family plans to ask Korin. No fixed travel time, extra power reading or numerical recovery increase is asserted.

facts.statement: The user directs that Goshin always master or perfect what he already has first. In deliberate training he develops his existing abilities to mastery or perfection before deliberately pursuing new techniques. When asked about Chapter Seven, the user chose the training-priority interpretation: Goshin may still copy instinctively in an emergency to protect someone. This does not retroactively make the first Kamehameha more practiced than Goku's (O088), erase his rapid-learning Talent, or give a new numerical power level. Mastery is attainable and retained; injury or fatigue can affect performance without deleting it.
facts.source: user creative direction and clarification, 1 November 2026
facts.source_class: user direction for authored OC

facts.statement: The user directs serious attention to foundations supporting Goshin's established abilities, such as stance, balance, movement, guard, breathing, conditioning, ki control and flight when relevant. These are examples rather than a fixed remedial program. Show practice and results without subtracting his prior strength or imposing a numerical ceiling; an older claim about a specific seated Chapter Seven exercise is not on the selected page.
facts.source: user creative direction, 1 November 2026; authored Chapter Seven application
facts.source_class: user direction and authored draft application
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: The user directs that Goshin focus seriously on his foundation. His continuing practice should give genuine attention to the basics supporting his abilities: for example stance, balance, movement, guard, breathing, conditioning, ki control and flight as relevant to the scene. These examples illustrate the direction rather than impose a fixed training program. Show repetition, correction and results, and honor what he already knows; do not replace his established capability with helplessness, a fixed growth cap or an invented number. In the revised Chapter Seven draft he carefully adjusts his footing and resolves to improve the Kamehameha he already knows; he is still injured and full practice waits for recovery.

facts.statement: Kanzenshuu's episode-7 guide and the Dragon Ball Wiki describe Gohan being chased by a dinosaur and stranded high on a rock while Piccolo observes, and Goku's near fall from Snake Way. The Wiki additionally attributes apples to Piccolo. These are secondary episode reports, not inspected footage; the two accounts do not establish every silent frame or exact climb, jump, apple placement or number. The directly read captions independently contain Gohan's call for help, inability to descend, sour apple and Piccolo's once-only help statement (C157).

facts.statement: In the local episode-32 captions, 08:28–09:15, Goku remembers Grandpa Gohan warning him to stay inside on a full moon because of a giant ape, and realizes that the creature that killed Grandpa and destroyed the tournament venue was himself. This realization is normally placed later than the authored Chapter Eight discussion; caption provenance and video remain unverified.

facts.topic: chapter eight — collection and family reunion
facts.statement: Selected Chapter Eight: Chi-Chi and Ox-King are travelling by truck when Krillin finds them on the road. Krillin carries Chi-Chi to the riverbank; Ox-King continues by truck. Chi-Chi reunites with both boys and Goku, and Piccolo departs. She was not picked up by Bulma's aircraft at the ninth marker in this selected draft.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight continuing O102 and O103
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and logistics
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: In the provisional Chapter Eight, Bulma lands the already-established aircraft on a clear stretch of road near the ninth marker. Chi-Chi and the Ox-King actually squeeze into its cabin; Bulma checks the vehicle's weight marking. The truck remains at the roadside. Both reach Kame House and reunite with the family. Chi-Chi learns that Goku and Gohan each ate a Senzu and are completely healed, with their strength restored; she learns that Goshin, who refused his bean, still has head and hand pain. No hospital or runway is introduced.

facts.topic: chapter eight — Goshin receives care and declines Senzu
facts.statement: In Chapter Eight Chi-Chi rewraps Goshin's fast-healing burned palm and plans a medical examination after his head injury. Goshin chooses to reserve the last Senzu, have Gohan take one and see a doctor; Krillin retains the last bean. In Chapter Nine Chi-Chi brings him to the village doctor, who checks his head and hand and gives warning signs. No doctor is flown to Kame House in this selected sequence.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight and Chapter Nine, following O103; selected unaccepted branch, no standing food rule
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and consequence
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Chi-Chi calls a village doctor who has seen the boys before; Bulma fetches her in the same aircraft from the agreed road marker. At Kame House the doctor examines Goshin, checks his eyes and memory, has Chi-Chi show the place where he was hit, cleans and wraps his burned hand, advises rest and urgent care for worsening symptoms, and plans a further check. His head still hurts, he has no dizziness at the exam, and complete recovery is not declared. He still refuses the third bean because he did not see it made; Roshi retains it, uneaten, in his pocket. Goshin watches Chi-Chi prepare the curry he eats. The doctor, trip and exact treatment are authored, not episode-7 canon.
facts.previous_source_before_story_and_nappa_c: authored Chapter Eight following O103 and the standing food rule

facts.topic: chapter eight — family choices and foundations
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Eight, both brothers speak about the dinosaur rescue and Gohan acknowledges fear. Gohan asks to continue his studies while the family prepares; Goshin tells Goku he wants to practise aiming. The selected page does not show the older seated-footwork exercise or a perfected wave.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight and the user direction
facts.source_class: authored draft staging applying user instruction
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Gohan remembers helping his brother and father, voices his fear, and asks to learn to protect his family while keeping his wish to study and be a scholar. His parents agree that no child is being sent away and will discuss a plan together. Goshin asks to make his existing Kamehameha reliable; with the doctor limiting exertion he voluntarily and briefly adjusts seated foot placement, following Goku's demonstration, and stops to rest. He does not practise a new technique, fire a wave, or perfect it on this occasion. This applies the user's mastery-first and foundational direction without blocking instinctive emergency copying or erasing the first-wave qualification (O104 O105 O088).

facts.topic: chapter eight — Kami, Popo and Piccolo
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Eight, Popo tells Kami that Piccolo pursued the boys and also stopped a dangerous animal; they do not excuse the coercion. Kami discusses Raditz's arrival in the afterlife, his uncertain feeling of about a year for the linked lives and the possible last Dragon Ball use. Piccolo trains alone after the confrontation. The conversation does not establish that Popo reports every Senzu detail.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight adapting episode-7 dialogue C128
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and character expectation
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: In the divergent draft, Popo reports seeing Piccolo try to take the boys while Kami was away and confirms that Goku and Gohan ate Senzu and are fully restored; the other boy refused his bean. Kami and Popo discuss Raditz's arrival in the afterlife, their interpretation of Piccolo, Kami's uncertain feeling of about one year for the linked lives, and the possible last use of Earth's Dragon Balls. Kami intends to send word to Korin; no message has yet been delivered. Piccolo trains alone in the wasteland with neither child and does not secretly feed or watch Gohan. Kami's feeling is not a guaranteed death or guaranteed last wish.

facts.topic: chapter eight — different Otherworld café message
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Eight, the Otherworld guide tells Baba that Kami asked Yemma whether King Kai might help living Goku and that Yemma would ask without promising an answer. Baba intends to tell Roshi; no permission or resurrection request is shown. The selected exchange does not state the older extra conditions attributed to Yemma.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight adapting the episode-7 guide and Baba scene C158 and following O100
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and conditional message
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: The guide tells Baba that Kami asked Yemma about King Kai for the living Goku, who was injured when Kami made the inquiry; Yemma requested recovery and willingness before considering it, and the road was only shown to Kami. The guide does not know about Goku's subsequent complete Senzu recovery. Baba intends to tell her brother Roshi that Kami has a question for Goku. No request from Goku to delay resurrection exists, no permission for the road has been granted, and Baba has not yet delivered the news.

facts.topic: chapter eight — dark scouter moved to lab
facts.statement: After the Chapter Eight riverbank reunion, Bulma capsules the damaged aircraft and keeps the wrapped scouter and its power cell separate. In Chapter Nine she opens the casing at Kame House without reconnecting the cell and decides she needs her lab. No powered test, translation, safe-transmission finding or new reading occurs there.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight following O093 and O102
facts.source_class: authored draft staging and device state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Bulma keeps the removed scouter cell separate, wraps the parts independently, and takes them in separate case compartments as she flies the doctor to the village and then plans to go home. The device has not been powered or decoded, and its transmitter has not been proved disabled. She intends to work on it at her lab; no reading or safely operating device is established.

facts.topic: chapter eight — evening plans and remaining Dragon Balls
facts.statement: Chapter Eight ends at the river clearing with the reunited family preparing to leave. Chi-Chi will take Goshin for a medical examination; the last Senzu is with Krillin. Gohan keeps the Four-Star Ball on his hat, while two other Dragon Balls were last at the mountain house. The older claim that the family spends that night at Kame House and boards its wall is not the selected scene.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight following the earlier continuity
facts.source_class: authored draft end state and open plans
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: The family and Ox-King spend the night at Kame House; Goshin still needs observation and a follow-up, and Goku can carry him and Chi-Chi to the mainland if urgent care is needed. The Ox-King's truck is still by the ninth road marker. Gohan's Four-Star Ball remains on his hat at Kame House; the family's two other balls remain at their mountain house. The family considers gathering or protecting the balls but has not done so. Ox-King, Gohan and Goku board up the wall Raditz damaged as a temporary repair; Chi-Chi covers the gaps inside with a sheet as a moon-safety precaution. Neither a particular long-term training plan, transport home, new dragon wish, perfected technique nor scouter reading is established.

facts.topic: chapter eight — moon warning and Goku's question
facts.statement: At the Chapter Eight clearing, Roshi tells the family that he saw Goku turn into a giant ape after looking at a full moon and apologizes for not saying so sooner. Goku asks whether he could have caused Grandpa Gohan's death; Roshi does not know. Roshi advises keeping the tailed boys from looking at a full moon. Chapter Nine then explicitly shows a full moon, but neither boy sees it or transforms.
facts.source: authored Chapter Eight response to the earlier C031 C075 warning and background C175 C176
facts.source_class: authored family conversation and precaution
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: After Raditz's island warning, Roshi tells the reunited family that he witnessed tailed Goku turn into a giant ape after seeing the full moon at the tournament. Goku learns this earlier than in the unchanged episode-32 realization and asks whether he could have caused Grandpa Gohan's death; Roshi was not there and does not claim certainty. Roshi apologizes for withholding what he knew, explains that he cannot be certain whether the boys would change, and advises them not to look at a full moon until they learn more. Chi-Chi closes curtains and covers the temporary wall's gaps; both children keep their tails. No present moon phase, transformation, tail removal or definitive answer about Grandpa is established.

facts.statement: A Kanzenshuu forum rewatch identifies Yajirobe's episode-8 vehicle as an aircar, and the Dragon Ball Wiki lists a hovercar among episode objects. These are secondary reports rather than an inspected full episode; the altered branch's exact route, second passenger and fit are authored.

facts.statement: The official Grandpa Gohan character showcase reports that Baba arranged his one-day return to fight and that he and Goku had an emotional reunion. It is manga-based background; it does not establish a new appointment, a new answer, or Baba's specific knowledge in this branch. Toei's original-Dragon-Ball episode-76 synopsis separately says Baba calls Grandpa Gohan back from the afterlife for one day and describes his emotional reunion with Goku (W-113); it is not complete TV footage or proof of a later new visit.

facts.statement: A secondary synopsis of Z episode 37 reports that Mr. Popo takes Bulma to Yunzabit on a flying carpet. This establishes only the reported later use, not its provenance, creation date or an episode-8 journey to Korin; the earlier placement in the altered story is authored.

facts.topic: chapter nine — the changed tower summons
facts.statement: Selected Chapter Nine: Kami sends Popo to Korin, who sends Yajirobe on Popo's carpet to Kame House with an invitation for Krillin, Yamcha, Tien, Chiaotzu and Yajirobe to prepare. Kami separately visits Goku's family at the doctor's. No earlier sighting of Goshin asking Roshi about watching a bean grow is needed to establish the message.
facts.source: authored Chapter Nine; adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Kami sends Popo to Korin, and Korin sends Yajirobe to Kame House. Krillin, Yamcha, Tien, Chiaotzu and Yajirobe are to gather at Korin Tower so Kami can train them; Goku is asked to speak with Kami, and his family is invited when Goshin can travel. The messenger also reports Kami's conditional King Kai inquiry without claiming Yemma's permission. Popo's earlier carpet trip, Yajirobe's specific aircar trip and the changed invitations are authored. No one has yet trained at Kami's or been compelled into custody. Before leaving, Popo is shown observing Goshin ask Roshi about watching a Senzu grow, establishing the information he later passes to Korin.

facts.topic: selected chapter nine — Baba’s conditional inquiry
facts.statement: Baba tells Roshi at Kame House that a guide said Kami asked Yemma about the living Goku; Yemma would ask but promised no answer. Roshi tells her Goku is with his family and was healed by a Senzu. Goku and his family are not present for that Baba scene. Kami separately tells the family of his inquiry later; no permission has been granted at that checkpoint.
facts.source: selected Chapter Nine, Kame House and mountain meeting; canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored selected review-branch event; not reader acceptance

facts.statement: HISTORICAL PROJECT NOTE, NOT SHOWN IN THE SELECTED CHAPTER NINE: earlier records attributed to Goku and Baba an on-page request to relay his uncertain Great Ape question and his sons’ names to Grandpa Gohan. The selected Chapter Nine and its protected pre-correction copy do not show that request or promise. The origin of the conflicting record is not established. Goku did ask Roshi whether he might have hurt Grandpa in selected Chapter Eight; no answer was known.

facts.topic: chapter nine — limited scouter test and Yamcha lead
facts.statement: Selected Chapter Nine: Bulma opens the scouter casing at Kame House, sketches the wiring and says she needs her laboratory before dismantling more. The cell remains out and the device is not powered. Bulma and Krillin leave for her lab first and plan to look for Yamcha afterward; they have not found him on-page. A powered 206 reading is a separate source-baseline or older-branch claim, not a selected Chapter Nine measurement.
facts.source: authored Chapter Nine; adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Bulma disconnects a suspected transmitter and microphone, translates the display and tests the scouter on an external supply inside a mesh enclosure with Krillin present. The original cell remains out. The device reports 206 for Krillin in this authored test, matching the baseline episode's number; his reading rises when he raises energy. She explicitly cannot guarantee that the shielding prevents an unknown alien transmission or that the reading is accurate, and powers the test off. The scouter is not cleared for open use. Bulma mentions seeing Yamcha's name in sports pages, and Krillin leaves intending to ask at the city stadium; he has not located or recruited Yamcha, Tien or Chiaotzu. Bulma explains that she has learned what she can with the device off and is now choosing a limited powered test despite the unresolved risk; this is not proof of safety or a claim that the original cell was replaced.
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: Selected Chapter Nine: Bulma opens the scouter casing at Kame House, sketches the wiring and says she needs her laboratory before dismantling more. The cell remains out and the device is not powered. She and Krillin intend to look for Yamcha, then go toward her lab. A powered 206 reading is a separate source-baseline or older-branch claim, not a selected Chapter Nine measurement.

facts.topic: chapter nine — family returns and doctor follows up
facts.statement: Selected Chapter Nine: the village doctor examines Goshin's head, quickly healing hand and ankle, cautions that one examination cannot reveal everything and says to return for concerning symptoms; she would like another look if they remain. At the covered bridge, Gohan volunteers Nimbus to reach Mina, Goshin flies and braces the broken board, and Chi-Chi, Goku, Ox-King and Mina's father contribute. Chi-Chi checks Goshin's symptoms afterward. The damaged bridge makes the family accept the doctor's offer of a room for the night. They do not go home or receive the older home-visit examination in this chapter.
facts.source: authored Chapter Nine; adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: After the doctor permits a gentle, monitored journey, Yajirobe takes Ox-King in his aircar to the ninth road marker. Gohan and Goshin ride Nimbus beside Goku, who carries Chi-Chi; Ox-King, Chi-Chi and both boys go home in the recovered truck with Goku flying alongside. At home the doctor checks Goshin's head and burned hand. He reports less head pain but is not declared recovered; warning signs, monitoring and another follow-up remain. No hard exercise, sparring or flight practice is cleared, and a long trip must wait for a further check. At home Chi-Chi brings out the previously promised schoolbag; the grandfather additionally gives Gohan an animal book and Goshin a puzzle. No agreement that Gohan will carry the bag is asserted.
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: Selected Chapter Nine: the village doctor examines Goshin's head, healing hand and ankle and says to return if concerning symptoms arise. At the covered bridge Gohan and Goshin help rescue Mina; Goshin flies and holds a board while Chi-Chi and Goku watch for symptoms. The damaged bridge makes the family accept the doctor's offer of a room for the night. They do not go home or receive the older home-visit examination in this chapter.

facts.topic: chapter nine — present Dragon Balls and moon precautions
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Nine Gohan still has the Four-Star Ball on his hat. Goku says two other Dragon Balls are at home and should be checked later; they are not shown being inventoried that night. The full moon appears above the damaged bridge and Piccolo hears Goku's warning, but the covered boys do not look up or transform. Later moon phase remains unspecified.
facts.source: authored Chapter Nine; adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: At home, the Three- and Six-Star Balls are checked and returned in a box to the cupboard; Gohan retains the Four-Star Ball on his hat. The family will ask Kami and Korin about safer placement, but no ball has been delivered elsewhere and no wish has been made. They cover the home windows at night. The moon remains intact, both children keep their tails, and no present lunar phase, Great Ape transformation or certain answer about Grandpa is established.

facts.topic: chapter nine — doctor’s meal and foundations
facts.statement: Goku and Gohan remain restored after the whole Senzu they eat in Chapter Eight. Goshin has not eaten one; Krillin retains the last. At the doctor's in Chapter Nine, Goshin brings bowls to the table, asks for eggs and eats with his family. The selected page does not contain the older physician-limited footwork program or establish a rule about watching food.

facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state

Goshin did not eat the third bean, which Roshi keeps; he watches Chi-Chi and Ox-King prepare the meals he eats. With the doctor's explicit limit he makes only a few gentle standing foot placements, corrects his heel and rests; stronger or longer training and flight practice remain unapproved. He wants to make his existing wave and foundational footwork reliable. This is mastery-first practice, not a new technique or a claim of perfected mastery; instinctive emergency copying is still allowed.

At the doctor's in Chapter Nine, Goshin watches Chi-Chi wash and cook rice and eggs before eating. The selected page does not contain the old physician-limited footwork program.

facts.topic: chapter nine — Gohan chooses to help and Piccolo trains alone
facts.statement: At the covered bridge in selected Chapter Nine, Gohan takes initiative with Nimbus to rescue Mina and her book while Goshin holds and secures the broken board. When Goshin offers to shoot the branch jamming the bridge, Gohan notices the pier in the line of fire; both move to a clear angle and Goshin precisely breaks the branch. Both parents and Ox-King contribute. Gohan chooses to retain the Four-Star Ball. Piccolo hears Goku's full-moon warning from concealment, not via an unearned earlier source. Gohan is not shown flying independently in this chapter; his exact first acquisition date is unspecified, and he demonstrates it by Chapter Thirteen (O176).
facts.source: authored Chapter Nine; adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_008.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-8 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: At home Gohan observes a small creature and works out how to free a bird without hurting its wing, then chooses a short, supervised step-back-and-call exercise with his parents nearby. His studies and wish to help remain his own; he has not independently flown. Piccolo trains alone against two targets in the wasteland, with neither child in his custody. No six-month solitary sentence, original outfit and sword, or unearned knowledge of Raditz's moon explanation is imported.

Gohan chooses to retain the Four-Star Ball. Piccolo independently hears the full-moon warning from concealment. Gohan does not yet fly independently.

facts.topic: episode 1 forest, hat recovery and city — secondary report
facts.statement: W-65 describes Gohan’s forest encounter and river rescue: the sabertooth takes his hat, Goku sees it on the cat, the frightened cat leaves it, Goku rescues Gohan on Nimbus and returns the hat to him. It then reports Raditz passing over a city before Piccolo. The local captions support the lost-hat dialogue and Goku questioning the cat, not the silent recovery, return, river or city images. Selected stills in W-127 show the cat wearing the hat, Gohan with the log and the father-son reunion; their source/cut are unverified and they do not show the whole sequence. The unaccepted chapter dramatizes the recovery and return.
facts.source: W-65 detailed episode-1 synopsis; W-30 captions; W-127 selected published stills
facts.source_class: secondary synopsis, redistributed caption text and selected fan-hosted stills

It then reports Raditz passing over a city before meeting Piccolo. The local captions support the lost-hat dialogue and Goku questioning the cat, but not the silent recovery, return, river or city images. The synopsis is secondary, not independently checked video; the user-authorized Chapter One revision now dramatizes the recovery and return.

facts.statement: The local episode-9 captions narrate about one year before the Saiyans, Gohan alone in the wilderness and Goku running in the afterlife toward King Kai. Gohan wonders how he got down from the cliff, recalls seeing the moon and says he remembers nothing after that; a caption explicitly names a sabretooth growl, and he notices his tail missing and clothes changed. Later growls, an eagle sound and cries for help occur. The waking image and complete animal choreography are secondary reports, not established by these words alone.
facts.source: redistributed Japanese episode-9 captions, 03:04–07:05; origin unverified
facts.source_class: caption text read directly; provenance unverified

facts.statement: At 07:47–08:33 Gohan recognizes an illustration of a Nemurian civilization vimana from a reference book and identifies a very old prototype capsule robot. At 16:59–17:11 he identifies an SSS-type universal capsule robot as number C-6 from a robot book. That knowledge is Gohan’s in the baseline; the caption does not establish manufacturer, precise appearance, or a complete visual survey.
facts.source_class: caption text read directly; provenance unverified

facts.topic: episode 9 robot asks for sleep; damaged sight
facts.statement: At 08:33–12:09 the awakened robot warns against loud voices because vibrations dislodge sand, repeatedly asks Gohan to switch it off and says there is an exit behind it. Gohan says the visual sensor is broken and offers to repair it; the robot initially objects. The captioned reply suggests it can see him afterward, but the exact repair and silent exit geography need a visual witness.
facts.source_class: caption text read directly; provenance unverified

facts.statement: At 14:59–18:14 Gohan repeatedly awakens the robot about a scorpion and hunger. It first tells him to stop; eventually it directs him to find food in the cave. Gohan asks it to cook and asks for a mother-style flavor; it tells him how to use its head and oven and he says the food tastes bad. The food’s visual identification as mushrooms is separately reported; the local spoken wording alone does not name it.
facts.source_class: caption text read directly; provenance unverified

facts.topic: episode 9 animal pursuit, ravine and food — secondary reports
facts.statement: W-69 reports an alligator, sabretooth, eagle and flying reptile preceding the desert fall, a steep ravine at the exit, and mushrooms cooked for Gohan. W-70 instead describes Gohan grabbing the large bird’s leg, while W-69 says the bird seizes Gohan; neither account is verified footage. W-67 and W-68 summarize the hole and buried robot. The local captions explicitly label a sabretooth growl and eagle call, but do not establish the full visual choreography or the named food.
facts.source: W-67–W-70 episode reports; redistributed Japanese episode-9 captions
facts.source_class: secondary broadcaster and rewatch synopses

facts.statement: At 18:20–19:29 the robot says an excavation accident and unstable ground buried it in the ruins about eighty years earlier. Gohan recognizes the Nemurian temple from a book and wants to free the robot. The robot says it intends to save energy and emerge on its own, objects to being disturbed and warns that Gohan’s digging will upset the balance.
facts.source_class: caption text read directly; provenance unverified

facts.topic: episode 9 collapse, wires and energy gas
facts.statement: At 19:32–24:17 the robot warns that the cave is collapsing, urges Gohan to leave, asks him to join blue and red wires in its head, calls for full power and tells him to go. Later it says it has used up its energy gas, urges him on, and becomes unresponsive as he calls to it. W-67 and W-69 describe it saving Gohan and being left behind; silent rescue choreography and any permanent-death diagnosis are not established by captions alone.
facts.source: redistributed Japanese episode-9 captions, 19:32–24:17, plus W-67 and W-69
facts.source_class: caption text with separately identified secondary visual accounts

facts.statement: The local episode-9 narration at 24:31–24:43 asks what next adventures await Goku and Gohan and notes the approaching Saiyans; it does not say Piccolo will be surprised. In the separate 25:57–26:22 preview Gohan asks about Tien and Yamcha and Goku wonders whether they know of his death. This is a preview, not evidence that either fighter meets anyone during episode 9. Ending music follows; a cue starting at 30:42 lies after the local ending and is excluded from the episode inventory.
facts.source: redistributed Japanese episode-9 captions, 24:31–26:22 and later cues
facts.source_class: caption text and separately inspected local boundary; provenance unverified

facts.topic: episode 9 Goku, cloud and animal framing — secondary rewatch
facts.statement: W-70 reports that dead Goku runs along Snake Way, wonders if he can eat a cloud and is later shown having eaten it. The local captions identify Goku saying he is hungry at 07:05, while later 15:30 and 16:36 cloud-hunger and satisfaction lines are not labelled by speaker in that file. W-70 also disagrees with W-69 about whether the bird first seizes Gohan or he grasps its leg; no episode video has been inspected to decide the staging.
facts.source: W-70 Japanese fan rewatch, W-69 independent rewatch and redistributed episode-9 captions
facts.source_class: secondary episode reports plus directly read caption text

facts.topic: chapter ten — examination, breakfast and journey
facts.statement: In selected Chapter Ten the doctor rechecks Goshin, permits normal movement and asks the parents to report changes. Goshin helps Gohan set the table and eats breakfast before the family looks for Mina's riverborne books; the boys are trapped beneath the bank with C-6. The old passenger-only tower trip and ban on independent flight are not the selected treatment.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: The doctor re-examines Goshin the morning after Chapter Nine and permits a gentle monitored passenger trip, not independent flight, running, heavy lifting or training; he must rest and report symptoms and needs another follow-up. The family visits Korin and Kami, stops to check him and returns home before late. He watches the raw food, cooking, packing, reheating and lemon preparation before the portions he eats; he does not eat a Senzu. Goku and Gohan remain fully healed and restored.

facts.topic: chapter ten — family safety, moon and Kami warning
facts.statement: The Chapter Nine family conversation with Kami covers his linked life with Piccolo, the uncertain one-year feeling, the possible Dragon Ball danger and Yemma's ungranted inquiry. The family keeps precautions during the visible full moon. Chapter Ten continues from the doctor's rooms; it does not send Goku to a desert survey while the others wait at the Lookout.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Chi-Chi and Goku choose to keep the family together on the journey, acknowledge Piccolo may find them and reject any guarantee of safety. Kami says his life is tied to Piccolo and shares his uncertain approximately one-year feeling, not a certain death date or wish. Goku tells Kami the moon warning; the family keeps its precautions. Yemma has granted no passage, Baba has given no answer, and Goku has not agreed to leave for King Kai. Goku temporarily goes to the desert only after the family explicitly weighs separation while Kami, Popo, Chi-Chi, Ox-King and Yajirobe remain with the boys.

facts.topic: chapter ten — book, carving and robot contact
facts.statement: Mina's machine book helps the brothers recognize the Nemurian carving. Gohan sees three S's on the buried robot; C-6 identifies his own SSS series. Goku and Chi-Chi search from outside, and the brothers speak through a slit. No desert survey crew, Lookout radio lesson or remote identification is shown.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Gohan and Goshin examine a machine book; Gohan asks about the Nemurian site and Popo tunes a regional survey bulletin about an unstable desert excavation. Goku volunteers, demonstrates controlled lifting and works under the survey crew’s directions. By radio Gohan identifies the likely SSS type, Goshin answers Goku after an explicit invitation and identifies the orientation of the old exit; Goshin remains at the lookout under his medical limits. The workers, bulletin and radio are authored, not episode footage.
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: Mina's machine book helps Gohan and Goshin identify the Nemurian carving and the buried SSS-series robot during their Chapter Ten search for her books. Goku and Chi-Chi search from outside; the brothers speak through a slit. No desert survey crew, Lookout radio lesson or remote SSS identification is shown in this selected chapter.

facts.topic: chapter ten — C-6’s consent and damaged sensor
facts.statement: Gohan switches on buried C-6, who wants to sleep, warns about noise and digging and recounts about eighty years trapped. After the blocked exit is found, the brothers wake him again. Goshin wipes the impaired eye only after C-6 agrees; it remains limited. C-6 later agrees to a supported rescue; Goku did not first activate him.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state

C-6 recounts about eighty years trapped, warns that digging can bring down the roof and agrees to an attempt after considering the plan. Goku clears loose sand only with permission; the sensor remains cracked and works imperfectly. The altered initial encounter and consent are branch staging.
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: Gohan switches on the buried robot C-6, who asks to be left to sleep, warns that noise and digging can collapse the chamber and describes his long entrapment. His eye is impaired. The brothers wake him again after finding the exit blocked; later C-6 considers and agrees to a supported rescue. Goku did not first activate him in this draft.

facts.topic: chapter ten — fallen beam and chosen rescue
facts.statement: Gohan draws out a wooden wedge despite C-6's warning, shifting the beam and roof; Goshin catches a falling stone. Goku holds the outer slab and Chi-Chi helps outside. The boys prop the beam; C-6 knowingly chooses to spend reserve despite a worsening leak and directs Gohan to connect the emergency wires. He catches Gohan as Goshin supports the beam with ki, and they extract him awake, with a bent arm and uncertain energy. No shutdown or repair is shown.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: An independent new tremor destabilizes the site; Goku holds a slab while C-6 agrees to a red-and-blue emergency connection, uses remaining energy to move and is carried out. This authored rescue and its different outcome depend on additional help. C-6 is responsive afterward but nearly out of energy, declines unauthorized reconnection and elects to be switched off. It is unknown whether he can wake; no refill or completed repair is asserted.
facts.previous_statement_before_dragon_ball_fe: In selected Chapter Ten, Gohan draws out a wood wedge despite C-6's warning, causing the beam and roof to shift; Goshin catches a falling stone. Goku holds the outer slab, the boys prop the beam and C-6 consents to Gohan connecting the emergency wires. Together they extract the still-responsive robot, whose arm and energy are damaged. He is not shown choosing shutdown.

facts.topic: chapter ten — robot at lookout and remaining threads
facts.statement: The Chapter Ten family and C-6 reach the village doctor's yard. C-6 remains awake with a damaged arm and uncertain energy; Goku offers to ask Bulma to inspect him and C-6 requires permission before anyone opens his panel. Mina, her father and the boys read with him. The older Lookout/shutdown handoff and lemon scene are not this selected ending.
facts.source: authored provisional Chapter Ten; episode-9 adaptation tracked in canon/SCENE_COVERAGE_009.md
facts.source_class: authored episode-9 divergence and current draft state
facts.previous_statement_before_character_cont: Popo agrees to keep C-6 quiet at the lookout; the survey office and possibly Bulma may be contacted, but no specialist has examined him yet. A little lemon is prepared in Goshin’s view for C-6’s suggested seasoning, which tastes too sour. The family returns to the mountain house with the Four-Star Ball on Gohan’s hat; the Three- and Six-Star Balls remain in the home cupboard, and no wish or tail change occurs. Krillin’s fighter search and the promised Chapter Eleven preview remain future work.

facts.statement: Chi-Chi, both boys and Bulma visit C-6 at the laboratory. Gohan lends him Mina's bridge book with the condition it be returned when he is finished. His arm and click/leak remain unresolved; Dr. Brief asks permission before inspecting.

facts.topic: chapter 16 review — island, storm and Piccolo
facts.statement: The family accompanies Bulma to a weather station. The boys make a raft, assist a trapped tiger and face a storm. Already able to fly independently, Gohan is washed underwater, releases the net and gathers ki to rise; Goshin reaches and lifts him clear while holding the branch easily with his ki. Bulma and Chi-Chi help clear the net; Gohan frees the loop. The raft drifts away. Piccolo senses both boys, initially thinks the Saiyans might have come early and asks them to train with him; the family refuses, and he leaves without taking them. They return home.
facts.source_class: authored selected review-branch event; not accepted canon or approval

The boys make a raft, assist a trapped tiger and face a storm; Goshin lifts Gohan from the water, and the raft drifts away. Piccolo senses the boys, visits and leaves after the family refuses his taking them; they return home.

facts.topic: chapter 17 review — seven children and first visit
facts.statement: At the Lookout Chi-Chi tells Kami that Piccolo thought the boys' ki might mean the Saiyans had arrived early and then asked them to train. The family finds the raft near an old town, meets Pigero, Rom, Chiko, Ena, Jink, Hatch and Yordon, intervenes when Ena is grabbed, and prepares supper. At the market Rom and Yordon take fruit and Chi-Chi pays for it; Gohan and Rom disagree. Chi-Chi offers a night at home; Pigero chooses to stay with the children that night.
facts.source_class: authored selected review-branch event; not accepted canon or approval

The family finds the raft near an old town, meets Pigero, Rom, Chiko, Ena, Jink, Hatch and Yordon, intervenes when Ena is grabbed, visits the market and prepares supper. Chi-Chi offers a night at home; Pigero chooses to stay with the children that night.

facts.topic: chapter 17 review — cuffs and one-night trial
facts.statement: The family returns with Bulma; workers and police arrive. Ena protests when the man who hurt her grabs Rom, and Gohan also intervenes. Pigero says the cuffs are too tight and asks for help. Goshin asks the officer to remove them, tells Pigero how he will bend the locks and carefully opens both while protecting his wrists; he checks for injury. The officer objects and takes the bent cuffs. Rom, Chiko, Pigero and Bulma inspect the home, and the six younger children choose one shared common-room trial night. Pigero may stay for supper; later placement remains open.

Rom, Chiko, Pigero and Bulma inspect the home; the six younger children choose to try one shared common-room night. Pigero may have supper; later placement and arrangement remain open.

facts.statement: In the local episode-17 captions, Piccolo begins direct training with Gohan and tells him to sense his target. The narration gives six months until the Saiyans in the source baseline; that countdown and Gohan’s isolation are not imposed on the divergent review branch.

That Lookout interval is not imported as an exact duration into the active branch.

facts.topic: selected chronology — Gohan flies before the chamber
facts.statement: In revised unaccepted Chapter Thirteen Gohan uses his own ki to lift and fly out of the closing fissure while his family is present. In Chapter Fourteen he flies on the riverbank with Chi-Chi watching and practises turns during a spar. Chapter Twenty-Two develops this existing flight under the room's gravity; Chapter Twenty-Three shows improved speed to a mother who already knows he can fly. The exact first learning date and teacher are not asserted.

facts.topic: selected chronology — Goshin integrates Kamehameha mastery and growth
facts.statement: Goshin sees Goku's wave once and first fires it against Raditz in Chapter Five under O088's first-use conditions. He later clashes with Goku in Chapter Thirteen, gains strength during the wave contest that remains after the wave, and wins their ring-out by adapting to his father’s wrist pull. He keeps moving stones stable while stopping his wave in Chapter Fifteen, and demonstrates deliberate shape, direction and stopping while teaching Gohan in Chapter Nineteen. In the full chamber year he applies that mastery alongside substantially greater strength and ki; in Chapter Twenty-Three he uses it in open sky while controlling eight moving blocks, comfortably beyond Piccolo in the ordinary spar and releasing more power he already had. Mastery is earned and retained, not a ban on further growth, an exact numerical grade or a permanent universal ranking.
facts.source: selected corrected Chapters 5, 13, 15, 19, 22 and 23; user training direction O104

facts.topic: selected correction — Chi-Chi and voluntary training
facts.statement: The corrected selected story gives Chi-Chi agency as a mother, martial artist and participant. In Chapter Fifteen she wins a first-to-two touch match against Tien, who restrains his ki for the exercise; the result is not a full-power ranking. She offers tactical observations, protects her sons' choices and remains concerned for their safety and education. In Chapters Nineteen through Twenty-Three the boys and Piccolo conduct and end their own exchanges. In Chapter Twenty-Three she plans with Popo and Bulma to help civilians away from fighting; no evacuation outcome is shown. The assistant-invented eye-blast breach is removed. facts.topic: selected review chronology — authored outside interval before the chamber
facts.statement: In the revised unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Two, months have passed since Goku began direct lessons at the end of Chapter Twenty-One, and nearly a year has passed on Earth since Raditz’s warning. This is an authored branch interval, not a source-proven exact number of days. Goku has practised Kaiō-ken and Genki-dama; the family has continued contact with the children, including a visit the previous week, and their director has asked them again and renewed their shared room as a temporary arrangement while seeking a lasting one. No confirmed school place, permanent placement, birthday or exact arrival date is supplied. The brothers then live a full additional year together in the chamber while roughly one outside day passes.

facts.topic: Gohan's original Saiyan-arc training and conditional power readings
facts.statement: The manga-based official profiles describe Gohan's 1,307 rage outburst against Raditz, six months surviving apart followed by roughly six months of Piccolo's direct training, and a 2,800 reading as he fires an enraged Masenko after Piccolo's sacrifice. They also describe Gohan's kick against Nappa and his later return, Genki-dama deflection and Great Ape contribution. These are source-baseline events; the outburst and Masenko readings are situational, not proven ordinary resting levels or maxima for every future context. They did not automatically occur in the altered branch.

facts.topic: episode 18 and 46: Goku pod damage and salvage
facts.statement: In the local episode-46 captions Goku first says Raditz's ship exploded and his own old ship was safe and was being repaired (12:06–12:34). Later, Brief's dialogue says the ship was found broken in pieces, crucial parts remained and almost all had to be rebuilt; Goku is surprised (18:04–18:28). Episode 18 identifies the pod as the projected moon's source; a selected still shows a beam striking it and a secondary synopsis reports its destruction (C207). The episode-46 account permits a possible salvage reconciliation, but the actual episode-18 visual aftermath and recovery were not verified; neither an intact discovery nor a definite contradiction is established. The selected branch instead preserves and covers the machine for Bulma, who has not yet identified ownership.
facts.source: Dragon_Ball_Z_018.srt and 046.srt; Kanzenshuu episode-18 guide and selected still; Toei episode-46 synopsis
facts.source_class: direct redistributed captions, selected still and separately labelled official and secondary synopsis; original footage and caption provenance unverified

facts.topic: episode 38–44 Namek departure and elapsed travel
facts.statement: In the local episode-38 captions Bulma estimates a month to Namek and initially five days until departure (08:38–08:49), then revises preparation to ten days to learn/input Namekian and the group agrees to meet at Kame House in ten days (13:25–13:38). Episode 39 calls it the seventh day of the journey. Episode 40's narrator places Vegeta at a Freeza base 18 days after he left Earth. Episode 44's narrator says Bulma's group arrives at the real Namek 34 days after they left Earth (17:03–17:12), not 34 days after the Saiyan battle. These are source-continuity clocks, not requirements for the divergent branch. In episode 60 Gohan says ‘nearly four days’ and asks whether the destination is still far (22:56–23:01), without explicitly naming the starting event. In episode 63 Roshi tells Bulma it is the sixth day since Goku departed (08:49–08:52). Episode 66 has Bulma tell Brief that six days have already passed while she asks when Goku will arrive (17:37–17:50); she does not yet know he has reached the battlefield. This is her trip-context statement, not an independently verified stopwatch or a basis for assigning the episode-60 'nearly four days' line an unstated start.

facts.topic: episode 54 Great Elder awakening latent power
facts.statement: In the local episode-54 captions the Great Elder gives Krillin a Namek Dragon Ball and awakens his dormant power; Krillin feels a large increase (09:02–11:46). Asked whether this could work for a small child, the Elder says it is possible for anyone who has dormant power and says his act merely triggers it without shortening his life (11:51–12:10). Krillin proposes bringing Gohan, and the Elder agrees (12:13–12:26). These are the Elder's statements and this intervention, not a numerical multiplier, proof of unlimited reserves or an automatic future invitation to the divergent twins. In episode 70, 12:05–12:17, the Elder tells Dende he has already drawn out Dende's power so he can travel quickly. The dialogue does not date or depict that intervention or establish exactly what later ability it caused.

facts.topic: episode 55 King Kai training and Piccolo group spar
facts.statement: In the local episode-55 captions Yamcha, Tien and Chiaotzu complete Bubbles and Gregory's exercises, then the three spar Piccolo together under King Kai (04:52–10:14, 15:45–21:37). The trio surprises weighted Piccolo; after they ask him to remove his weights, King Kai stops the spar before another exchange. The captions establish neither an unweighted rematch result nor an individual human-over-Piccolo ranking. These dead-warrior source circumstances and their training do not determine the earlier divergent brothers' author-directed post-chamber advantage.

facts.topic: episode 61 Gohan awakening and Vegeta comparison
facts.statement: In the local episode-61 captions Krillin privately doubts his earlier suggestion that the Great Elder could make Gohan Vegeta's equal (04:25–04:32). After the Elder awakens Gohan's ability, Krillin senses his ki rise, and Vegeta remarks that his basic power rose sharply and later says it is still insufficient to fight him (11:21–15:32). Vegeta's self-assessment is not a measured multiplier or a completed fight, and no future branch ranking follows.
facts.source_class: direct redistributed Japanese caption dialogue; original source, cut and full footage unverified

facts.statement: In the local episode-65 captions Chi-Chi is distressed that Gohan is in danger, says she will go save him; Brief asks her to hear his operating explanation, and she asks which is the launch switch (07:01–08:37). Brief says he built this second ship in two days. Later he addresses her on regaining consciousness as she cries for Gohan (23:13–23:29). A secondary episode guide describes her entering the craft, an attempted launch and a crash, but the exact visual cause and staging were not independently viewed (W-93). This is evidence of active maternal concern as well as her educational priorities, not a demand that the divergent branch repeat the accident or fix her capabilities. In the same local TV-caption account she remains determined to reach Gohan in episode 88, Dr Brief reports repairs completed (04:58–06:44), and episode 89 describes converting the craft from one to five seats and filling it with energy (09:01–10:45). An attempted group launch fails in episode 90 (17:41–20:18); Toei's episode-90 synopsis separately confirms the failure (W-109). Captions and synopsis alone do not verify its visual cause. In episode 107, Brief's repaired craft is ready for the rescue party, but he says Bulma has already reported everyone back and they do not leave; Chi-Chi reunites with Gohan on Earth (07:35–09:04). The scene does not require the divergent branch to reproduce the attempted journey.
