facts.topic: Gohan detects body-change impostor and acts
facts.statement: In episode 72 the local captions have Gohan and Krillin sense approaching evil ki; when a person with Goku's appearance arrives, Gohan warns that it is not his father and says he knows despite not understanding how (16:20–19:27). In episode 73 Gohan briefly hesitates to strike his father's apparent body, apologizes, accepts Krillin's reassurance and fights beside him (06:26–08:16). Episode 75 also has Gohan cheerfully imagine himself a great fighter in new clothes (05:07–05:46). These are distinct emotional, perceptive and playful moments, not a universal detection power or a mandate to reproduce the encounter.

facts.topic: Ginyu Body Change and acquired-body control
facts.statement: The local episode-71 captions state that Ginyu injures himself and exchanges bodies with Goku (20:05–23:59); Goku's unfamiliar, wounded body impedes his flight. In episode 73 Jeice reads 23,000 for Ginyu in Goku's body (05:00–06:05); Goku says coordinating mind and body is necessary to use greater power and Kaiō-ken. Later Goku and Krillin think Ginyu is becoming more accustomed to the body, while Goku also adapts somewhat (19:04–20:54). Episode 74 reverses the swap when Goku intervenes in an attempted change, and Goku says Ginyu ended up as the frog; W-104 separately reports the manga account and frog interception. The events do not establish an automatic complete skill transfer, a precise adaptation rate or an unavoidable branch outcome. In the separately bounded original-Z TV account of episode 89, Bulma makes a translator for the frog, the device voices 'Change,' and Ginyu occupies her body while she is in the frog (20:09–21:46). In episode 90 Ginyu in Bulma's body reaches the fight, while the others initially misunderstand; the ending raises a threat to Piccolo, unresolved at the episode-90 checkpoint. In episode 91 Ginyu attempts Change on Piccolo but Bulma regains her own body and Ginyu becomes a frog again; Toei credits Gohan with throwing the frog and intercepting the attempt (04:41–08:00; W-110). Toei's episode-89/90 synopses also report the TV swap (W-109). Do not silently import that additional sequence into an unreviewed manga version or assume a branch outcome.

facts.topic: Namek Dragon Balls initial limits and later upgrade
facts.statement: In the local episode-75 captions Dende says Namekian is required for the password and wishes (19:21–19:35); he summons Porunga. In episode 76 Porunga offers three wishes within his power but rejects a request to revive a group, saying he can revive only one person per wish (04:08–05:10). Piccolo is revived first and sent to Namek second; the Elder dies before the third and Porunga vanishes. In episodes 99–101 Earth's separate dragon revives Freeza's victims, the Elder briefly returns, and Porunga reappears to grant the previously unused third wish; Dende uses it to transport the people on Namek except Goku and Freeza to Earth (C267). The Elder then appoints Mūri before dying naturally again in episode 105. Episode 107 states a 130-day recharge and shows later, individually granted Namekian resurrection wishes and a relocation (C270). The separate official manga-based Porunga feature reports that a later Great Elder upgrades the dragon to remove the one-person restriction and describes a later 130-day recharge (W-103). Do not apply this earlier limit or recharge universally to all dragons, times and versions, or force these wishes in the divergent branch.

facts.topic: Namek warrior types differ by source and moment
facts.statement: In episode 70's retained captions three Namekians say they too are warrior-types like Nail, and Freeza reports each around 10,000 before their confrontation (19:30–20:07). By episode 77 Nail calls himself the planet's last warrior-type (10:05–10:13). A separate Dragon Ball Official manga-based Nail profile describes him as the planet's lone warrior-type (W-108). Keep the anime's earlier three and Nail's later claim distinct from the manga-based summary; do not merge the versions or assume a number of surviving fighters in the changed branch. facts.statement: In episode 77 Nail proposes assimilating with Piccolo, saying it can make Piccolo's power several times greater; he reassures Piccolo that Piccolo's personality remains. Piccolo, initially unwilling to lose his own identity, agrees, and reacts to a large increase (09:05–16:19). In episode 81 the caption labels Nail speaking to Freeza within the encounter, 'I have assimilated with Piccolo,' followed by a Piccolo-labelled explanation of the power increase (19:07–20:34). This is a caption speaker attribution; without the original audio and visuals it cannot settle how an independent voice or consciousness is staged or whether it persists. The manga-based Nail feature describes the assimilated Namekian surrendering body and personality, while a separate official editorial speculates Nail may nevertheless influence Piccolo later (W-108). Neither Nail's estimate nor the editorial settles an exact universal multiplier, definitive future mental state or all other fusion mechanics. In this branch Piccolo is presently alive; no Namek journey or meeting is fixed.

facts.topic: Goku, Ginyu and Freeza Namek power statements
facts.statement: In the local episode-69 captions Goku calls Kaiō-ken before Ginyu's scouter count rises (22:28–24:59); episode 70 has Ginyu report 180,000 and Goku say his instantaneous power can rise further (06:09–06:32). Jeice had described Ginyu's maximum as 120,000 (03:57–04:05). In episode 71 Freeza reports Nail at 42,000 and says his own power is 530,000 while not intending to fight at full power (10:27–11:10); in 78 he says his transformed power is certainly over one million (20:16–20:33). W-104 separately reports the manga-based 180,000 Kaiō-ken event. These are specific scouter/contextual and character claims, not measured stable bases, a proven Kaiō-ken factor, universal conversion or later branch ceiling.

facts.statement: In episode 66 Goku tells Krillin not to explain but to let him probe; after a largely music-labelled interval he says he understands the party's increased power, Bulma's safety, the Dragon Balls and Freeza (10:23–11:30). Krillin is surprised and Goku says he simply felt he could do it. The captions alone do not establish exact contact, a technique name, an earlier acquisition date or an unlimited or infallible mind-reading rule; a secondary description or verified visuals would be needed for staging.

facts.topic: Namek fight Kaiō-ken and Freeza percentages
facts.statement: In episode 90 Freeza claims half his maximum would be enough to defeat Goku (06:01–06:07), later says he is using less than one-third (20:54–21:01), and King Kai says Goku is already using tenfold Kaiō-ken; the narrator repeats that tenfold usage (23:06–23:14, 24:24–24:31). In episode 91 Goku stakes a twentyfold Kaiō-ken Kamehameha on the fight, and episode 92 has King Kai judge that twentyfold exceeds Goku's limit (15:25–15:39, 22:36–24:37; 92, 09:51–09:57); Toei's synopsis reports an injury to Freeza's hand. These are claims, source-specific actions and a narration at those points, not exact independently measured power values or a basis for back-calculating a stable scouter base. The selected branch’s earlier Chapter 22–23 practice did not state a multiplier; the later corrected Chapter 32 has separately authored times-two and times-three uses (O249).

facts.topic: Ginyu Force fight on King Kai’s planet
facts.statement: The local original-Z TV captions have the four dead Ginyu Force members fight Yamcha, Tien and Chiaotzu on King Kai's planet; the humans initially hesitate, then recognize their training gains and defeat the group (93–95; especially 94, 09:12–11:34 and 95, 09:01–11:45). facts.topic: Gohan protects Piccolo and chooses to return
facts.statement: After Freeza injures Piccolo in episode 95, Gohan says he will fight for him; Goku says Piccolo is barely alive and tells Gohan to carry him away. In 96 Gohan worries about Goku's escape, thanks him and leaves (95, 20:44–24:23; 96, 06:11–07:15). In episode 100, believing his father dead, he asks Bulma to take Piccolo to Earth and returns to delay Freeza so he will not follow the Saiyans there; Goku reappears and orders him away (09:15–10:13, 17:48–17:54, 22:29–25:06). In 106 Gohan later resists Vegeta until Piccolo intervenes. These source-specific choices demonstrate independent concern and resolve; they do not require the branch to repeat the fights, deaths or apparent deaths.

facts.topic: Earth Shenron’s group wish and the Elder
facts.statement: In the local episode-99 captions Kami says Earth's contemporary dragon can revive a group with a shared condition, but the discussed group wish covers only deaths within a year and cannot undo natural death. He tentatively thinks an indirectly shortened lifespan might be restored for the time lost, expressly without certainty (08:17–09:44). King Kai proposes reviving Freeza's group's victims so the Elder returns and Porunga's remaining wish becomes available. In 100 Shenron says victims of Freeza's group on Namek have returned; the Elder and Dende return and Porunga reappears. In 105 the Elder appoints Mūri and dies naturally again; Vegeta claims the village he personally killed was excluded by the wish's wording. The tentative reasoning, actual result, character attribution and separate Earth/Namek dragons must remain distinct.

In 101 he insists the rescue wish exclude himself as well as Freeza so he can finish their fight. In 103 he declares the fight over, tells Freeza to live and tries to leave; in 104 he shares ki with the defeated opponent after Freeza pleads; after a further attack he retaliates in 105. These choices combine affection, competitive desire, anger and mercy in a particular sequence; they neither prove perfect control at every moment nor compel the divergent branch to reproduce the circumstances.

In episode 49, Dodoria discloses Freeza's responsibility and Vegeta says he had not known while being used since childhood (21:46–24:32). Episode 2 has Raditz give Goku the meteor account (C043). The later retrospective sits in direct tension with the earlier accounts; a community rewatch also flags it (W-112). Caption tags and secondary commentary do not verify the visual framing or establish a definitive reconciliation, whether either character lied, or what the early branch family knows.

facts.statement: In local Z-106 King Kai worries that reviving Goku and Krillin at destroyed Namek would leave them in space, based on his then-current belief both died. In 107 Vegeta proposes moving their souls to Earth first. After 130 days Porunga brings Krillin's soul, says Goku is alive and so his soul cannot be called, revives Krillin and restores his body, then reports Goku has refused a transport request; Yamcha is revived as the third successful wish. After another 130 days Chiaotzu and Tien are revived individually and the Namekians relocate (106, 18:47–19:50; 107, 04:53–05:36, 10:13–10:38 and 15:22–24:14). These are bounded, time-specific results, not a universal rule for every dragon or branch.

facts.statement: In the original-Z TV captions Freeza says Namek will explode in about five minutes after damaging its core (97, 21:58–23:16); later characters and narration give successive smaller estimates, including roughly three minutes in 100 and under two or one in 101–103. Events continue across several extended episodes. These are contextual statements and dramatic pacing, not an independently verified real-time stopwatch, an exact episode-duration equation or a mandatory deadline for the divergent branch.

facts.topic: original-DB time room versus later Z chamber
facts.statement: Toei's original-Dragon-Ball episode-129 synopsis says Goku travels to the past through a 'room of time' (時の部屋). The separately read selected original-Z episode-147, 155 and 168 captions concern the later Room of Spirit and Time and its stated limits (C234 C235 C236). The short DB synopsis and translated name alone do not prove the two are the same room or definitively different rooms. The selected branch's mental exercise and later physical chamber year are separate authored events.
facts.source: Toei original Dragon Ball episode-129 synopsis; selected Dragon_Ball_Z_147.srt, 155.srt and 168.srt cues

facts.statement: Toei's original-Dragon-Ball episode-85 synopsis says Yamcha and Krillin did not participate in the previous tournament, but its own episode-21 synopsis describes Krillin's match and episode-22 synopsis describes Yamcha's. Selected live pages confirm the conflicting text. This is a contradiction between publisher descriptions, not a verified contradiction between the underlying episodes; do not use the episode-85 claim to revise the branch's established history.

Neither statement fixes exact birthday dates or the divergent twins' lived ages; their separate pre-Saiyan physical chamber year is authored.

This later original-TV exchange does not establish an earlier appointment or determine Piccolo's branch choices.

facts.topic: Garlic Jr return and earlier stated history
facts.statement: In the original-Z episode-108 local captions Popo recalls Garlic Jr being sealed in his own Dead Zone; Garlic claims Dragon Ball-granted eternal life and says Goku and his son interfered (14:21–16:43). Episode 109 says he wants revenge and searches for Gohan. These are television characters' stated backstory, not independent verification of every scene in a film or proof that the altered family lived a movie unchanged.

facts.topic: Aqua Mist, antidote and similar water names
facts.statement: In original-Z episode 110 Garlic's follower says Aqua Mist becomes irreversible after 24 hours from inhalation, even with the antidote, and says a contaminated person's bite has the same effect (07:20–07:51, 17:26–17:37); other characters describe its use in that story. The Z antidote is called 超神水, as is the dangerous potential-revealing water described in Toei's original-DB 115–117 synopses. The similar earlier 超聖水 of DB 61–62 is described as ordinary water whose pursuit was training. Similar names alone do not establish that the substances or effects are interchangeable, nor does a villain's explanation prove a universal cure rule.

facts.statement: Episodes 110–112 present Piccolo and Krillin as apparently corrupted by the mist's bite; episode 112 reveals that both were acting and they free Kami and Popo (23:09–24:17). Episode 113's flashback has Piccolo tell Krillin a plan to hurt Gohan so Garlic approaches, and Gohan says the act fooled him (05:51–07:06). Toei's earlier 110/112 synopses preserve the apparent-corruption suspense. The captions do not establish exactly why the bites did not produce the expected effect, whether Gohan knew beforehand, full physical choreography or universal immunity.

facts.topic: Makyo Star and Garlic Jr claims
facts.statement: In the local Z-110 and 113 captions Garlic's follower and Garlic describe the Makyo Star approaching Earth every 5,000 years and increasing their power by tens of times; the follower says Garlic used the increased power to escape the Dead Zone. Garlic claims eternal life and episode 116 shows the group using a different strategy against him. These are particular characters' claims and conditional TV events, not measured universal numeric multipliers or proof of an unrestricted immortality rule.

facts.topic: Kami and Popo risk the sacred realm
facts.statement: In local Z-113 captions Popo proposes spreading antidote through seven currents and warns that entering the former guardians' sacred realm may cost Kami his position or life. Kami chooses to go; Z-114 dialogue links his plight to Piccolo's condition, and in Z-115 Kami entrusts the water to Popo. Z-116's recap says they have delivered it to the air-current opening. Their specific crisis is not a universal rule for every later afterlife or an inevitable branch outcome.

facts.topic: Gohan shield and team defeat of Garlic Jr
facts.statement: In Z-116 captions Gohan holds a shield against the Dead Zone and refuses to drop it because Piccolo and Krillin could be lost (08:00–11:04). Toei's episode-116 synopsis says Piccolo and Krillin leave the shield and Gohan takes the opportunity to aim at the Makyo Star. Later dialogue says its destruction deprived Garlic of supporting power and sent him into his own Dead Zone (22:48–23:35). Piccolo's claim that Gohan ought to have sufficed alone is his judgment; this cooperative later event fixes no branch power multiplier or required sacrifice.

facts.statement: The local Z-117 captions call Turtle's birthday his 1,000th; he describes the Mermaid's Tears' happiness as a legend. Gohan asks Krillin to leave the pearl cherished by fish, and Krillin agrees. Later Krillin says goodbye to Marron because he doubts he can make her happy; she says she might have married him and leaves. The imagined wedding and consideration of a proposal are not a completed proposal or marriage.

facts.statement: The official Z-117 synopsis describes Krillin, Marron, Turtle and the pearl, then appends an unrelated account of Goku and the exploding Namek disappearing. Z-107's local captions establish that Goku is alive, and Toei's Z-107 title also says so. Do not treat the stray publisher fragment as a new episode-117 event or proof of Goku's death; it is an editorial-source defect, not a finding that the episode itself contradicts its story.

facts.topic: chapter 23–24 scouter, confrontation and Namekian name
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Three, Vegeta scans two distant signals at 9,200 and 12,400 without identifying their owners. In Chapter Twenty-Four he scans approaching signals at those values again, then identifies the readings with Gohan and Goshin in the city. Four other approaching signals display 1,120, 1,360, 1,410 and 700 without on-page target identifications; Vegeta compares them with the brothers before departing. Piccolo and the twins confront the Saiyans; Vegeta recognizes Piccolo's voice from Raditz's transmitting scouter and requests the Dragon Balls. Nappa identifies Piccolo as a Namekian from Planet Namek; Piccolo does not claim to have made the Balls. Vegeta accepts Piccolo's proposed quarry while seeking the Balls, a saleable world and information about the brothers. Nappa reports a changed Goshin reading at the quarry before removing his scouter; Vegeta keeps his on. Gohan quietly suggests asking Kami later; Kami is not shown hearing the exchange.

facts.topic: chapter 24 Vegeta’s attack, released power and positions
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Four, Goshin decisively overpowers Nappa in the city, and Gohan separately restrains Nappa when he threatens civilians. In the quarry Vegeta attacks Piccolo and Krillin; the brothers combine their Kamehamehas to redirect the attack into empty sky. The collision's shock loosens a wide slab. Goshin catches and carries it clear while Gohan redirects smaller debris; with Vegeta still a threat, Goshin releases more previously held-back ki and keeps the higher output ready after the light settles. Neither the wave nor the slab confers a fresh permanent increase. Four Saibaimen are alive, one pinned, and Vegeta is preparing another attack. Goku continues training with King Kai before departure; Yajirobe starts down Korin Tower. No maximum, new form, immunity or predetermined victory is established.

Gohan independently helps clear smaller debris and defeats a different attacker. Goku continues the real return on Snake Way. Yajirobe starts down Korin Tower. This is retained situational growth, not a measured maximum, new form, immunity or predetermined victory.

facts.topic: author correction — released output versus actual growth
facts.statement: The author rejects Chapter Twenty-Four's implication that Goshin permanently gains roughly 4,000 power simply by firing one Kamehameha; the earlier lower reading can reflect his not yet releasing all the power he already possessed. Anger and being pushed hard are examples of circumstances in which Goshin or other characters may increase their power, not mandatory triggers. The author rejects a numerical ceiling, fixed rate or rigid rule that only extreme situations allow development. Goshin's innate whole-being Adaptation Talent and potential for very rapid, substantial combat growth remain. Apply character, context and causality without treating every ordinary action as an automatic permanent gain. The selected revisions remain unaccepted.

facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Five Goshin defeats the Saibaiman pinned at the previous endpoint, leaving three. Piccolo catches another for Tien and Chiaotzu, who defeat it. A third grapples Yamcha; he senses its rising ki and directs his existing ki ball under it, carrying it away before it self-destructs overhead. Krillin pulls Yamcha clear. Piccolo throws the last creature into the air and Krillin destroys it. Yamcha has a minor forearm cut. All six originally grown Saibaimen are accounted for; no canon Yamcha or Chiaotzu death is imposed.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Five Gohan intercepts Nappa as he attempts to attack the other fighters, prevents his blasts and ground attack from reaching them, and physically overpowers him. He turns Nappa’s mouth blast skyward and uses his learned Kamehameha against him at a bare quarry wall. Nappa falls unconscious but remains breathing; Gohan moves a falling slab away from him. Piccolo and Krillin later carry Nappa clear of Vegeta's line of fire and shield him from debris; Piccolo wants to question him about Namek. This does not fix Nappa’s later fate.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.topic: chapter 25 Goshin and Vegeta readings and battle growth
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Five Vegeta reads Goshin at 16,300, then 19,400 after Goshin deliberately releases more of the power built before this fight. Vegeta recalls his earlier concern about Kakarot's children and recognizes that the new reading is above the power he had been using; this comparison establishes neither Vegeta's maximum nor a new numerical reading for him. He clips away the scouter, raises his own ki and fights Goshin, whose first punch pushes back his guard. During the subsequent sustained exchange Goshin feels real further growth in ki and strength, holds a later kick that had previously pushed him back and lands blows; no numerical gain, fixed growth trigger, maximum or final Vegeta result is established. The earlier 3,100 increase between the displayed readings is released reserve, not a newly acquired permanent gain from one attack.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.statement: Chi-Chi, Puar and Popo continue helping people at the bus. Bulma takes the mother, father and daughter to the gym. A volunteer says a driver with an injured arm is being treated, but the identity is not conclusively established on-page. Bulma calls Roshi from the gym and reports Chi-Chi’s sighting of Krillin and Yamcha heading west; she does not claim to see the fight. Puar stays to help by choice. Later Chi-Chi sees violet and blue light in the western sky, remembers the brothers' training and steadies a passenger; she cannot see her sons. Full evacuation and citywide casualties remain unknown.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.topic: chapter 25 selected frontier and remaining battle
facts.statement: At the unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Five endpoint all six Saibaimen are gone, Nappa is unconscious but breathing, and Vegeta remains active. After Goshin intercepts Vegeta's full-power Galick Gun, Gohan joins him and their combined Kamehamehas drive it back into the open sky; Vegeta breaks off and avoids the wave. Goshin then presses him, Gohan follows, and their first shared physical impact against Vegeta occurs before the endpoint. Piccolo and Krillin are at the western wall with Nappa; Piccolo wants to question him about Namek. Tien, Chiaotzu and a lightly cut Yamcha are together beyond the tracks. Goku remains with King Kai, preparing his target test; Kami’s Yemma meeting and Goku’s return are not shown. Yajirobe was last descending Korin Tower; the boys retain their tails and no form or final Vegeta outcome occurs.

facts.topic: Saiyan-arc Vegeta's Galick Gun and Earth threat
facts.statement: Dragon Ball Official's manga-based Vegeta profile identifies Galick Gun as his signature technique, describing condensed ki fired from the palms in a distinctive stance. In that separate source, wounded pride and anger prompt Vegeta to threaten Earth despite his earlier Dragon Ball goal; Goku counters with a Kaiō-ken-times-four Kamehameha. Toei's original-Z episode-31 synopsis separately describes Vegeta firing a full-force Galick Gun at Goku and Earth and Goku answering with a Kamehameha. Selected retained episode-31 Japanese caption cues name ギャリック砲 and include the threat to Earth; the source and cut of those captions are unverified. The original confrontation is later and differently staged; these accounts do not establish an attack number, fixed outcome or full audiovisual review for the divergent branch.
facts.source: Dragon Ball Official Saiyan-arc Vegeta profile; Toei episode-31 synopsis; selected Dragon_Ball_Z_031.srt cues

facts.topic: chapter 25 Vegeta's Galick Gun and the brothers' response
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter Twenty-Five, after Goshin's demonstrated growth and Nappa's defeat, Vegeta sets aside his wish for the Dragon Balls and commits all the power he can muster to a Galick Gun aimed at Goshin and Earth. Goshin intercepts it with his established Kamehameha; Gohan independently joins him with his own learned wave. Their combined attacks stop the descent and force the clash upward, and Vegeta cuts off his attack and moves aside. The combined light continues into open sky; Vegeta remains active. The pressure tears rock and rails loose, other fighters protect the unconscious Nappa from debris, and Chi-Chi sees the flash from the city without seeing her sons. This authored outcome does not assign a numerical Vegeta maximum, a fixed technique multiplier, a rule that either brother could not succeed alone, a new transformation or an ultimate Vegeta defeat.

facts.topic: original Z Power Ball and transformed Vegeta
facts.statement: The retained episode-31 captions (21:23–22:33) give Vegeta's account of Blutz-wave exposure through the eyes and an artificial moon created with a Power Ball and atmospheric oxygen; Goku notices Vegeta's ki decrease as he produces the light. The retained episode-32 dialogue (08:18–08:24) says Great Ape Saiyans have ten times battle power; Toei's short episode-32 synopsis independently describes Vegeta's tenfold strength. Dragon Ball Official's separate manga-based profile identifies the Power Ball. These sources do not establish a permanent multiplier for the author's evolving Goshin or dictate the altered branch, a present natural-moon phase, complete visuals or a fixed outcome.

A separate official game/manga commentary describes the disc as useful against stronger opponents; do not turn its promotional wording into an absolute all-target guarantee. facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 26 Goshin and Gohan continue fighting Vegeta together, applying their prior strength and independent choices. Vegeta fires toward the unconscious Nappa after hearing Piccolo wants answers; Gohan protects the people carrying him while Goshin presses Vegeta. Tien, Yamcha and Chiaotzu move Nappa into a sheltered gully; he remains unconscious and breathing. Krillin retains the unused whole Senzu. No numerical maximum or final outcome is established.

facts.topic: chapter 26 artificial moon and enemy choices
facts.statement: Vegeta notices both brothers retain tails and makes a Power Ball despite its ki cost, gambling that the boys would lose control and endanger their allies. Piccolo warns them; both turn away, while Vegeta looks and consciously transforms. The natural moon remains intact and its current phase is unspecified. Vegeta intercepts Gohan's attempt, guided by Piccolo, to hit the artificial moon; this does not establish whether it could be destroyed if reached.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.topic: chapter 26 coordinated defenders and Gohan choice
facts.statement: Tien uses Solar Flare and Krillin throws his cutting disc at Vegeta's tail; Vegeta hears it and moves his tail, so the disc cuts the ridge instead. Piccolo and Gohan keep the falling slab from the gully. Gohan then attacks the artificial light using Piccolo's directions, but Vegeta intercepts. After discussion Gohan decides not to look, independently helps the others, remains involved in the fight and deflects Vegeta's aim; no Gohan transformation or fixed maximum is asserted.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of unaccepted branch

facts.topic: chapter 26 first conscious controlled Great Ape
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 26, having protected his friends and knowing the prior moon warning, Goshin deliberately looks at Vegeta's artificial full moon. From the beginning of his first transformation he remains aware and controls his footing, tail, speech and choices. He feels the unfamiliar first-form power while his body responds naturally and the strength in him continues building. He senses his brother and friends, catches Vegeta's attack, directs falling rocks away with ki and pushes him toward empty ground. His ordinary clothing and shoes tear during the change; his tail remains. He is still in the giant form at the endpoint, facing active transformed Vegeta. No compulsory fear, new scouter reading, fixed form multiplier, golden or divine form, a separate normal-sized ape mode, or ultimate battle outcome is shown.
facts.source_class: authored continuation following standing first-form control direction

facts.topic: chapter 26 city, Launch, Yajirobe and Goku
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 26 Chi-Chi, Bulma, Popo and Puar continue helping civilians; Chi-Chi notices the artificial light and plans with Bulma to approach the quarry after the immediate rescue. Launch returns to Bora and Upa at Korin Tower asking after Tien; Yajirobe comes down, Upa lends him a flask, and he and Launch drive toward East City without reaching the quarry. Goku is still practising the gathered sphere with Gregory and King Kai; they have not seen the landing. Kami's meeting, Goku's arrival, a complete evacuation and casualty count remain unshown.

facts.statement: The retained episode-33 dialogue has Krillin plan to cut the tail while the opponent is distracted (07:02–07:05), later includes Vegeta reacting to his lost tail (12:19–12:22), and has Goku say he will transfer the energy he gathered from Earth to Krillin while Gohan fights (22:18–22:57). facts.statement: The retained episode-34 dialogue names the Genki-dama held by Krillin (05:33–05:52) and has Goku urge Gohan to bounce it back, saying it is on their side (12:58–13:05). facts.topic: chapter 27 controlled giant fight and further growth
facts.statement: In the unaccepted continuation Goshin remains conscious in his first giant form and stops transformed Vegeta’s descending fist one-handed after earlier using both hands against a giant fist while ordinary-sized; the earlier action does not establish that both hands were necessary. His existing strength continues developing during the sustained exchange; his body responds to the power of his first Great Ape experience, contributing to additional genuine growth without a number or universal compulsory trigger. Vegeta uses a thrown slab and an attempted tail grab as tactics; Goshin and Gohan divert the slab. After Vegeta targets Chi-Chi, Goshin redirects his mouth-fired attack with his controlled giant-form Kamehameha and Gohan independently blocks the follow-up. The previous Galick Gun remains a real named threat.

facts.statement: Gohan independently proposes another shot at the artificial light. Piccolo directs his lowered-face aim, and Goshin agrees despite not knowing whether he will revert and holds Vegeta away from the firing line. Gohan’s Kamehameha breaks the Power Ball; both Goshin and Vegeta revert, their tails intact. This result and its immediate effect are authored branch staging, not a claim of separately verified original-Z episode footage. Gohan does not transform; no exact multiplier, new scan or natural-moon phase is established.

facts.topic: chapter 27 Vegeta defeat, Nappa awakening and scouters
facts.statement: Vegeta continues fighting after reversion and attempts a dust-screen attack and a grab at Gohan’s tail. Both brothers counter; Goshin feels that fighting and his first giant transformation have left his ordinary-sized body and ki much stronger than before he looked at the light, and Piccolo senses the increased ki. Goshin uses his accumulated unnumbered strength to knock Vegeta unconscious, catches him before the wall and checks that he is breathing. Krillin watches the prince. Piccolo removed Vegeta’s scouter and placed it on stone out of reach without touching its controls; earlier Krillin removed Nappa’s and kept it in an outside pocket. Nappa wakes injured in the gully, learns Gohan and Piccolo’s account of Vegeta firing at him, and is guarded by Gohan, Tien and Chiaotzu. Piccolo asks about Namek; no answer, long-term custody, pod use or escape is shown. Krillin retains the unused whole Senzu.
facts.source_class: authored continuation; exact unaccepted endpoint

facts.statement: Chi-Chi, Bulma, Popo and Puar finish removing the people found in the damaged building; Chi-Chi reports unchecked rooms and the next street to volunteers, and an officer drives that way. No complete citywide evacuation is claimed. Bulma calls the children’s-home director, who says all six remain together in the hall, and calls Roshi with limited news. The group approaches the quarry; Chi-Chi witnesses controlled giant Goshin, later covers him with the gym blanket and checks both brothers. Bulma and Puar reunite with Yamcha, whose minor forearm cut remains. Goshin reports a sore side and has cheek and shoulder marks; Gohan has a sore shoulder and a glancing hip blow, without diagnosis.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of the wider response

facts.statement: Launch and Yajirobe help free a truck obstructed by metal and continue toward East City using the lower road; the city and quarry have not been reached, and Yajirobe still has Upa's flask. On King Kai's planet Goku aims at Gregory's falling twig. King Kai prepares a brick target and says he will check on the Saiyans afterward. Neither has been shown learning about Goshin's change or the fight; Goku has not left for the return, and the Yemma meeting and family reunion have not happened.

facts.statement: At episode 2, 16:36–16:57, the retained caption sequence has an inquiry after Krillin, a warning to Goku that the stranger is not normal, and a response that merely facing him is frightening and that this has never happened before. The individual lines here lack speaker tags; their contextual Goku–Krillin attribution is also described in W-43, not directly labelled by the caption. facts.topic: chapter two emotional and original-anime evidence pass
facts.statement: In the unaccepted local Chapter Two revision, Gohan remembers the river while flying above the sea, finds courage to greet Goku’s friends and is frightened when Goku admits fear of Raditz. Goshin reassures Gohan during introductions, learns about their father’s training, attempts to go to injured Krillin and chooses to stand before Gohan after Goku is felled. Bulma keeps the boys close; Gohan puts his hat on again before Goshin straightens it. Goku asks after Krillin, admits his fear while holding his ground, reflexively denies the children before warning Raditz away, and is explicitly backed by his friends. The two-child reactions, dialogue and blocking are authored; C300 records the distinct bounded source exchange. No fight, knockout or abduction is moved forward from Chapter Four and no power ceiling is established.

The moving signal shows an authored repeat of 334 during the Nimbus sea crossing, and 334 appears again on Goku at the island; 400 flashes without a named target before his later 400 scan of Goshin. Those added early power displays are branch snapshots, not source-proven numbers at those moments or maxima. The exact emotional-pass Chapters One–Two are preserved in the 1–2 pre-clarification ZIP. The separate 1,450 Goshin first-wave snapshot remains. Raditz guards the lens, assesses changed output and responds to the children. These numbers are specific branch moments, not canon measurements, fixed growth, baselines, ceilings, guaranteed maxima or damage formulae. facts.topic: original Z episode 37 medical treatment, pod and Popo
facts.statement: In the retained episode-37 dialogue the recovering group discusses medical treatment and a later Senzu crop (04:55–07:01). Bulma operates a device while watching a Saiyan pod on television; a reporter says the pod exploded, and Bulma wonders whether she pressed a self-destruct control (07:45–09:31). Popo later recounts Kami’s childhood in Yunzabit, proposes the former home might be a ship, and helps Bulma test voice commands (10:21–25:21). The text does not alone establish all silent staging, authenticity of its source/cut, or any corresponding altered-branch event.

facts.topic: chapter 28 Nappa’s Namek claims and Piccolo’s question
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 28 Nappa tells Piccolo he has seen Namekians on another world, identifies Namek as their planet, says he has not visited it and cannot give its location without a ship, and repeats Vegeta’s earlier suspicion about unusual abilities and Earth’s Dragon Balls. These are Nappa’s authored statements, not independent confirmation. Gohan proposes asking Kami, but Kami is not shown receiving or answering the question. No Namekian Dragon Ball set, coordinates or trip is learned or established. Nappa also claims the two scouters can summon the Saiyan ships; no one tests that claim.
facts.source_class: authored divergent continuation; no source knowledge automatically transferred

facts.topic: chapter 28 awakened Vegeta, guard and bean
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 28 Vegeta wakes, demands that injured Nappa rise and points a hand toward him. Gohan puts himself between them; Goshin restrains and redirects Vegeta’s raised arm, using the substantial, real and unnumbered strength he retained from the fight and first Great Ape experience. Stone cracks under the wrist, and Goshin eases his hold while keeping the injured prince restrained. Vegeta explicitly treats Nappa as expendable; Nappa remains injured and hostile, not an automatic ally. Krillin retains the only whole Senzu while Gohan seeks safe ordinary medical help. The two scouters are placed together on the stone out of the Saiyans’ immediate reach without pressing their controls; transmission states are unknown. No new scan or long-term custody is established.
facts.source_class: authored divergent continuation; no measurement or fixed growth rule

facts.topic: chapter 28 Launch, Yajirobe, city and flask
facts.statement: Launch and Yajirobe reach East City, see two dusty round objects in separate landing craters behind police barriers, help free an injured shopkeeper and continue to the quarry. Launch reunites with Tien and Chiaotzu. Yajirobe retains Upa’s flask, sharing some water for Goshin’s cheek and drinks; he pours a capful for Gohan to offer Nappa, who takes it. Neither traveler operates the objects; their internal condition, functions and longer custody remain unknown. No total city casualty or completed evacuation is asserted.

facts.topic: chapter 28 Bulma, civilian response and children
facts.statement: Bulma takes Yamcha and Puar back to the gym; his forearm cut is cleaned and dressed. A volunteer reports the lower room clear and an upstairs check still underway. Bulma warns against approaching the injured Saiyans without a fighter, asks a medical coordinator to discuss safe care and warns an officer not to operate the landing objects; a technical team has been called, but neither its inspection nor medical arrival is shown. She tells Roshi the local fight stopped and the brothers are with Chi-Chi; Goku has not returned at the time of that call. The director reports the six children still together in the hall and Hatch asking after the brothers. No permanent placement, citywide safety or final casualty count is established.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of shown local responses

facts.topic: chapter 28 Goku’s return, reunion and belongings
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 28 Popo retrieves the bags, places the target page and Hatch's drawing with the shared letter, tells Kami the family is at the quarry and returns the bags; the day-count page remains on the Lookout bench. Chi-Chi places the folded blanket in Launch's car before Bulma departs. After Goku completes the target test, King Kai discovers the early arrival, reports that the fight has stopped and immediately alerts Kami. Goku carries his supply capsule, uses Kaiō-ken along Snake Way, meets Kami at Yemma's office, returns through the arranged passage to the Lookout and flies to his family. Goshin describes his controlled giant change and retained gain; the old shirt and spare trousers fit imperfectly and he is barefoot. The letter remains folded for home reading. Goku mentions the capsule; it is opened in Chapter 29. No exact speed, new power reading or instant shortcut is asserted.
facts.source_class: authored continuation of the prearranged living-Goku route

Goku reaches Yemma’s end by the road, meets Kami at the office, returns through Yemma’s arranged passage to the Lookout and flies to the quarry. He senses the sons’ distinct increased ki and reunites with both and Chi-Chi. Goku and Goshin inspect his retained supply capsule without showing food removed or eaten. No instant return from King Kai’s planet or new fixed power reading is asserted.

facts.topic: author-directed first Great Ape and lasting hybrid-adaptation growth
facts.statement: The author clarified that Goshin became very strong through his hybrid inheritance and growth, innate Adaptation Talent and other existing factors, and that his first Great Ape transformation is itself a real new experience for the Talent. In the corrected unaccepted Chapters 26–28, his body responds to the unfamiliar power, and the sustained battle and first transformation produce a substantial genuine increase in physical strength and ki that remains in his ordinary body after reversion. Piccolo senses the greater ki compared with before the first transformation; Gohan later also senses it, and Goshin restrains injured Vegeta while deliberately controlling his pressure. The ordinary-body gain is real power, not merely better control, temporary size or access to previously held-back reserves. The Talent did not begin with this transformation, and its whole-being scope and future growth continue. No new scouter measurement, fixed multiplier or separate named normal-sized Great Ape mode is assigned; the latter is not prohibited or subject to an invented mandatory delay. This is Goshin-specific author-directed branch continuity, not a claim that every Saiyan receives the same effect.

facts.topic: chapter 29 independent city rescue and retained post-ape power
facts.statement: In the revised unaccepted Chapter 29 the city crew has heard someone upstairs. Gohan independently chooses a rear-window approach, calls down to the crew and carries the consenting trapped woman to safety. With Ren’s agreement, Goshin lifts the broken stair, landing and masonry, a broader and heavier load than the quarry rock he carried before his first transformation. He balances it on one arm while his ki independently holds the fractured wall and a falling brick; the crew then braces the section. His body and ki carry the substantial lasting growth from the fight and first controlled Great Ape experience. This is a qualitative comparison between shown actions, not a numeric maximum, fixed multiplier, proof of his former limit or an additional gain from the rescue. Other building areas remain unchecked, and an inquiry about the woman’s neighbour has no shown answer.

facts.topic: chapter 30 Kami’s account and the Yunzabit home
facts.statement: In revised unaccepted Chapter 30, Piccolo tells living Kami Nappa’s limited Namek claim. Kami does not recognize the name and recounts being alone at Yunzabit, a letter to wait for family, a possible head injury and an unusual home. A clearly bounded earlier Kami–Popo conversation and Kami’s memory dramatize the child waiting, growing up and leaving; neither the present boys nor Piccolo experiences that private recollection. Gohan suggests Bulma’s help; Goshin and Popo retrieve her. Kami, Bulma and Popo reach Yunzabit by carpet, with Piccolo and both brothers following Kami’s ki at extraordinary speed. Piccolo speaks the door word and the entry platform lowers, then rises. Bulma examines the interior; Gohan suggests voice control, Popo knows words, and Bulma separately recalls hearing disguised Kami and Piccolo speak an unfamiliar language at the tournament. The boys return to ask their parents; with Chi-Chi’s conditional permission, Goshin, Gohan and Piccolo accompany Bulma and Popo for a Jupiter test while Kami waits at Yunzabit. The ship reaches Jupiter; Bulma’s speech accidentally summons a toilet and a bed. No Namek coordinates, Namek journey, ship return or completed homeworld inquiry is shown. In the corrected Jupiter flight, both boys know the moon danger, turn away from unchecked views and see Earth and Jupiter only after Piccolo checks the window; they do not look at possible moons.

facts.topic: chapter 30 pod accident and device custody
facts.statement: In revised unaccepted Chapter 30, Bulma leaves Dr. Mori at the city gym and takes Yamcha, Puar, both captured scouters and their separate cells to Capsule Corporation. After officers report the landing sites cleared of personnel, she powers the Nappa scouter and tests a suspected remote command while watching one landing site on television. One Saiyan pod explodes; Bulma identifies an unintended destructive command or response as a possibility. The other object remains at its separate crater outside that view; its condition and controls are not verified. Bulma asks Dr. Brief to tell the officers what happened and keep clear of the other craft; he agrees. Popo and Goshin then invite Bulma to examine Kami’s old home. Yamcha, Puar and Dr. Brief remain at the lab. No new personal scouter reading or definitive answer about prior and current transmissions is established. The Chapter 29 neighbour inquiry is not resolved on-page in this revision.

Bulma keeps the captured scouters and their two separately wrapped found cells in her closed case, speaks with her father by telephone and intends a lab examination; no lab arrival, active scan or test is shown, and hidden power and past transmissions remain uncertain. Mrs. Endo at the gym identifies her neighbour as Mrs. Taki; a volunteer verifies the rescued woman’s name at the building and tells Taki that Endo is at the gym. facts.topic: author-directed world power and speed framework
facts.statement: The author clarifies that present Goshin, after the Saiyan fight and his first conscious Great Ape experience, is capable of destroying Earth; his substantial real ordinary-body and ki growth remains. The author places Goku at light speed or faster already during original Dragon Ball and directs that the world’s speed and power be written consistently with that interpretation. This is the author’s selected-branch baseline, not a newly measured exact speed, scouter number, fixed multiplier, unconditional constant travel speed or claim that Goshin destroys a planet on the page. Controlled actions and injuries remain possible, but may not turn planetary fighters into mundane humans. Both brothers retain agency and growth and Goshin is never less capable than Gohan.

facts.topic: author correction — deepening whole hybrid bloodline and emotional power
facts.statement: The author clarifies that when he directs Goshin's bloodline to become purer, deeper and stronger as Goshin grows through his developing Adaptation Talent, he means his entire Saiyan–Earthling hybrid bloodline, not only its Saiyan component. Both parental heritages are part of that developing whole, not a Saiyan side that grows while the Earthling side merely survives. This is Goshin-specific authored continuity, not verified real-world genetics or a universal canon rule; no fixed percentages, equal growth rate or molecular mechanism are specified. Like Gohan, Goshin has meaningful latent power that emotions can help release, expressed in his own personality alongside excitement, compassion, fear, anger and other feelings. Selected unaccepted Chapter 6 connects fear and anger to the existing authored 1,500 release; Chapter 25 gives emotional force to the ki surge during Vegeta's attack; Chapter 27 now describes strength inherited from both parents deepening together during his conscious first Great Ape. The substantial ordinary-body growth retained after reversion remains real. These are not claims that Gohan shares the separate Talent, that every emotional spike becomes permanent, or that rage, fear, a numerical multiplier or loss of control is compulsory. Preserve Gohan's independent choices and growth and the standing authored comparison (`O243`). The author additionally confirms that the hybrid bloodline itself is being refined and evolving, not merely producing more present strength; its inherited qualities and potential may deepen and form distinct expressions as the developing Talent and the rest of his being interact with life and experience (`O244`). The Chapter 27 sentence is one limited expression, not the definition or full demonstration of that growth.

facts.topic: chapter 33 traps, children and unresolved standoff
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 33 Bulma tests bay air and checks the clamps, Goshin bends one easily, and the group seeks the people and controls rather than risking an occupied hull. They rapidly handle corridor guns and corrosive liquid. In a sealed vestibule Gohan flies Bulma clear of an opening toward space, Goshin forces the hatch halves shut, and Piccolo removes the motor before the inner door opens. At a tempting table Gohan catches a knife, Goshin holds the descending dome, Piccolo stops the claw and Bulma gets clear. Armed children emerge; Gohan intercepts a shot without injury and prevents another child taking a loose gun, while Goshin suspends six weapons safely. All four travellers are free in the larger vessel, but the children control the exit; the children’s names and history, ship release, trust, meteor events and actual Namek arrival remain unshown. No full artificial moon or unaided-space survival is demonstrated.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon

facts.topic: Kaiō-ken multiplication and source-specific limits in original Z 29–31
facts.statement: The retained Episode 29 captions have Goku call Kaiō-ken without a number (15:56–16:04) and explain that he controls and temporarily amplifies his ki, increasing strength, speed, destructive power and defense (17:09–17:32). King Kai warns that losing control can damage Goku and advises at most twice his power at that point in his training (18:18–18:51); this advice concerns that Goku and situation, not a universal limit for Goshin. Episode 30 explicitly gives times two (19:26–19:28) and times three (22:10–22:14); Episode 31 gives times four (16:01–16:06). A call without an audible factor is not itself evidence of a particular factor. These caption cues are provisional and do not measure or rank the divergent branch.
facts.source_class: directly read redistributed Japanese captions; original source, cut and complete audiovisual performance unverified

facts.topic: official overview of Kaiō-ken as temporary ki amplification
facts.statement: Dragon Ball Official describes the Kaiō-ken as controlling and temporarily amplifying ki to increase power, speed, destructive capability and defense, and identifies Goku as the first successful user in its original-series account. This separate manga-based feature supports the broad mechanism but does not give current numerical levels for the divergent family, establish the factor of an unnumbered anime call or prohibit a later authored Goshin use.
facts.source: Dragon Ball Official, Learn Cool Kanji with Dragon Ball, Lesson 4, 7 July 2021; https://en.dragon-ball-official.com/news/01_277.html
facts.source_class: official franchise feature, manga-based; not full anime footage

facts.statement: The retained Japanese Z 45 cues around 18:19–18:59 have Zarbon report his old scouter failing around Vegeta rising above 22,000; Dodoria describes his as a newer model and reads 24,000. Z 47 reports three fighters increasing from roughly 1,000 to 3,000. Z 65 reports Gohan momentarily exceeding 20,000; Z 67 says a very brief rise may not be picked up. These are contextual observations, not a universal model limit.
facts.source: W-30, selected Z 45, 47, 65 and 67 cues; W-145 official Dodoria profile separately
facts.source_class: redistributed Japanese caption text, source/cut unverified; separate official manga-based feature

facts.topic: Freeza source self-statement and Nail reading
facts.statement: The retained Z 71 cues at 10:27–11:14 have Freeza read Nail at 42,000, state his own battle power as 530,000 and say he does not intend to use full power against Nail. This is source dialogue in that first-form encounter, not a scan of the divergent branch or a limit on later transformations.
facts.source_class: redistributed Japanese caption text; original source and cut unverified

facts.statement: Kanzenshuu’s source-separated battle-power list attributes Dodoria 22,000 and normal Zarbon approximately 23,000 to Daizenshuu 7. The list is a secondary report of guidebook values; it is not a spoken Z 47 measurement. The branch stages its own Dodoria scan at 22,000.
facts.source_class: secondary source reporting guidebook figures

facts.topic: Freeza, Dodoria and Zarbon — bounded voice evidence
facts.statement: The official Freeza leadership interview characterizes his speech as refined and courteous; the official Dodoria profile describes a hot-headed fighter, and the official Zarbon profile provides character context. These are source-informed characterization guides, not a rule imposing one English translation or a specific line in this divergent branch.
facts.source: W-147 official Freeza interview; W-145 official Dodoria feature; W-148 official Zarbon feature

facts.topic: retained Japanese honorific occurrences and translation boundary
facts.statement: Retained Japanese caption members for Z 45–49 contain polite forms including ドドリアさん and ザーボンさん in relevant scenes. The unlabelled subtitle text and contextual speaker attribution do not establish an authenticated cut, original audio or a mandatory English rendering. A secondary recollection reports an English version rendering the address as Mr. Dodoria, but its recalled quotations are not verified by original audio; the author rejects that wording in this working story.

facts.statement: The official 42-panel manga-volume retrospective describes Goku using ×10 and ×20 Kaiō-ken against Freeza on Namek, and describes depleted strength after the latter. Separately, retained Z 90–92 caption cues identify the same named factors in their own source context and King Kai judges Goku’s ×20 beyond his then limit. Neither evidence set establishes a universal ceiling, a branch Goshin number or a forced outcome.

facts.statement: Kanzenshuu traces an explicit hundredfold Kaiō-ken claim to a contemporary Weekly Shōnen Jump film-promotion poster and a later movie digest narration, while reporting that the Japanese movie itself names Kaiō-ken without voicing ×100. This is an identified secondary investigation of separate promotional/movie materials, not an original-anime TV claim, an independently viewed full film or a universal maximum.

facts.topic: author-requested Chapter 32 Kaiō-ken and power audit
facts.statement: The author flagged the missing Kaiō-ken multiplier and questioned the power depiction, requesting a comprehensive check. The corrected unaccepted Chapter 32 specifies Goku times two and Goshin times two and times three as authored scene choices, not factors prescribed by the author. It accounts for Goshin’s 19,400 pre-growth snapshot, his genuine subsequent fight/first-ape growth and his Earth-destruction-capable ordinary body. The factors apply to the unboosted output chosen for the exercise, and the times-three use is not an extra tripling of the times-two state. Goshin is holding back and redirects the spar himself; Goku is also using chosen sparring output, so the action does not declare their unknown full-power ranking. The temporary boost and independently retained, unnumbered ordinary-body/ki growth are distinct. No exact new scouter reading, compulsory strain, fixed future multiplier ceiling, new transformation or author acceptance is invented. At the audit checkpoint the interrupted Chapter 33 cabin use was aligned to times two without presenting the then-partial draft as complete; the author subsequently asked to continue, and resumption is recorded separately (O250). Prior versions and the accepted original Chapter 20 remain protected; caption review is not complete audiovisual review.
facts.source: Author request, 7 November 2026; selected unaccepted Chapters 32 and 33; canon/KAIOKEN_POWER_AUDIT_2026-11-07.md
facts.source_class: author concern plus authored revision and bounded source/continuity audit

facts.statement: After the author said to continue, the previously interrupted Chapter 33 was read through, reviewed against its source/branch coverage and finished as an unaccepted local review draft. Gohan independently chooses to practise the initial ordinary ki-gathering exercise Goku demonstrated and then works on his own fighting turn; no Gohan Kaiō-ken activation is claimed. Goshin briefly uses times two on deliberately small unboosted cabin output and retains real unnumbered growth separate from that temporary multiplier, alongside substantial post-fight/first-Great-Ape growth. The family, living guard, covered ship window, three retained tails, Piccolo and Bulma remain causally active. In the larger ship the travellers are free while the children control their vessel and exit; Gohan says learning to fly and fight does not make them soldiers, and Goshin asks whom the frightened children fear. facts.topic: chapter 34 collaborative meteor rescue and Goshin growth
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 34 the seven guns are set visibly aside by the children’s choice. When a meteor swarm threatens their vessel, Zeshin brings Bulma to the bridge and teaches her its controls; they steer together. Gohan independently opens the jammed sleeping-room door, lets Bun carry Naro, catches metal and seals a leaking pipe with focused ki. Piccolo protects children and checks a tightly framed image before tailed Goshin looks. From inside the intact hull, Goshin directs his ki beyond it to divert a large rock and several others. His ordinary strength deepens during the work and remains after he releases the rocks; this is real unnumbered growth, not merely released reserves or temporary Kaiō-ken. It adds to earlier substantial growth and does not prove unaided-space survival, a new form, maximum, fixed rate or compulsory trigger.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 34 children, attack history and distinct choices
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 34 Zeshin names Freeza and reasons from the travellers’ conduct; Bun remains distrustful even after the rescue and later takes one gun while keeping it pointed down. Miri and Naro are authored branch children, not verified identifications of unlabelled source characters. Bun’s dramatized memory shows his father, an attack by armoured strangers who invoke Lord Freeza, the evacuation and ships under fire. He saw his father fall but cannot know every survivor’s fate. Zeshin and Bun report no tails on the particular attackers they saw, not on all possible attackers. The children seek a former trading partner but do not know if they will be received. Bulma and Zeshin tighten a loose sensor connection after a sealed outer section is damaged; the ship is not certified safe. The travellers offer some supplies and the children choose to release their ship. Gohan tells the children that his father and the others were watching the injured Saiyans when the travellers left; he does not claim present secure custody or knowledge of later events.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 34 Earth guard and limited consensual care
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 34 Dr. Mori revisits Nappa under guard; he consents to cleaning and a dressing for his scrape, refuses needles and accepts water. Vegeta independently asks whether she can get him fit to fight, permits a limited stethoscope examination of his side without needles or transfer and ends it when he chooses. She cannot promise recovery or determine the full injury; Goku and Krillin protect the route while Tien and Chiaotzu remain with Nappa. Vegeta stays hostile, the cover is not secure custody, and Krillin retains the whole Senzu. No full diagnosis, safe transfer, escape or later outcome is shown.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

Krillin retains the last whole Senzu. Goku recalls his sons and presses Vegeta about unnamed dangers without learning Freeza’s name from the ship. No full diagnosis, safe transfer, escape or later outcome is shown.

facts.topic: chapter 34 departure, warned route and unconfirmed planet
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 34 the children release Kami’s ship and depart separately toward uncertain refuge. Miri points out KS162 on an old chart and Zeshin explains a current warning; Bulma copies the star pattern and uncertainties and chooses her course with Piccolo. After entering the displayed part of a current, Bulma steers through it and finds an unidentified green-and-blue planet and unread ship warning. They have not landed or confirmed Namek. Both boys retain their tails and avoid unchecked views; their bags and shared letter are aboard, with reduced unspecified provisions. Bun has one gun and the other six remain beneath the dome. No false-planet inhabitants, second Dragon Ball set, guaranteed route or return is established.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 35 route warning, landing and cliff
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 35 Bulma tests the destination display and notes separated course marks; her best interpretation is a course warning, not a complete translation, a name or proof of the world’s safety. With Piccolo she chooses a closer approach for directions, checks air within the sampler’s limited scope, and pilots a landing. Piccolo checks the visible sky for the tailed brothers. A ledge collapses; Gohan moves a slab away from two strangers, Piccolo carries Bulma clear, and Goshin supports and lands the ship without an incapacitating crash. The people claim the planet is Namek, but that identity is not verified.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 35 retained ship-hold growth and perception
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 35 Goshin uses substantial already-retained power and distributed ki beyond the hull to hold the entire falling ship without crushing it. His power and fine sense of the broad load and its separate pressure points develop during the work and remain after he releases it; he later feels along the hull while moving small stones. This is real unnumbered growth, neither a new maximum nor a temporary Kaiō-ken factor. He remains in sampled breathable air, and no unaided-space survival, compulsory psychic immunity, fixed rate, new form or general sensing range is established.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 35 alleged Namekians, radar and apparent spheres
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 35 the two strangers call themselves Raiti and Zākuro and claim the world is Namek. They offer an elder and a chart; Piccolo seeks people and information about Kami and says they are not entitled to take others’ possessions; Bulma seeks directions. She has packed her Dragon Radar but does not know whether it works on an alien set. Goshin volunteers to guard the ship, agrees a two-pulse ki signal and notes that Raiti’s small vehicle has his father’s name though the group did not tell the strangers. Raiti produces an apparent five-star sphere from a lake; Gohan carefully lifts an apparent two-star sphere from a ruin. Both are in Bulma’s bag for the alleged elder. Neither their nature, ownership, star count beyond what appears, wish power, hosts’ identities nor planet identity is verified.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 35 independent investigation and immediate confrontation
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 35 Gohan proposes leaving an apparent sphere in an old resting place until an elder can be asked, reports that his hands passed through an apparent animal at a marsh, and confirms his own ki still moves an ordinary stone. Piccolo refuses a risky suit dive; Gohan independently tries non-contact retrieval and lifts mud, not the third sphere. Goshin guards the hatch when its access catch moves twice with Zākuro nearby and sends the prearranged two-pulse signal. The party reunites; Bulma removes the radar cell yet reports a continuing beep that Gohan and Piccolo do not hear. Piccolo and Gohan question the strangers as grass and trees appear to move oddly. No confession, established identity, physical mechanism, third ball or final confrontation outcome is shown.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 35 Earth guard, memory and family visit
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 35 Vegeta remembers Goshin's conscious giant form and Gohan's destruction of the artificial moon. He considers using Goshin against stronger Freeza and suspects the travellers may have gone to Namek; a local Dragon Ball set remains unconfirmed. Goku and Krillin watch him while Tien and Chiaotzu stay by Nappa. Chi-Chi brings a repaired shirt and offers food and water; Vegeta takes the food but leaves the bottle during this scene. He has not escaped, and the provisional watch and whole Senzu remain.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 36, Piccolo, Gohan, Bulma and Goshin continue questioning the two apparent hosts beside the guarded ship. An apparent funnel, birdlike trees, a giant and a castle appear while Raiti tries to draw the party away. Gohan tests the apparent wind with a stone and protects Bulma. Zākuro moves the access catch and a real stone toward Bulma; Gohan catches the stone and restrains Raiti while Goshin prevents Zākuro reaching the hatch. The tailed boys avoid the unchecked sky and do not transform.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 36 retained body and ki growth under illusion
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 36 Goshin briefly starts toward an apparent Gohan in danger. The actual Gohan catches his arm; Goshin compares touch and familiar ki with the apparent figure and holds Zākuro and the access catch. His body and ki genuinely deepen again while he steadies his hold; the strength and clearer sense of the group remain after he eases his output. Prior substantial first-ape and ship-hold gains remain. This response is not universal psychic immunity, an exact sensing range, numerical maximum, fixed rate, compulsory trigger, new form or completed unaided-space survival.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 36 exposure and bounded stranger claims
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 36 Raiti and Zākuro reveal different reddish-pink bodies and admit they are not Namekians. The two apparent starred spheres in Bulma’s bag are shown as stones. The pair admit projecting images and a radar sound, reading thoughts and intending to take the ship; they claim they were stranded by a wreck and that mist marks a gap in a surrounding current. Their wreck, current, full capacities, privacy promise and the planet’s actual identity are not independently established. Bulma keeps the radar cell separate; no actual Namekian balls or compatibility is confirmed.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 36 shore animals and conditional investigation
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 36 real animals emerge from the nearby water and pull Zākuro. Gohan rescues him, Piccolo turns a limb away from Bulma, Goshin moves a larger animal with controlled ki and Raiti distracts another. Gohan asks to investigate the alleged wreck; Bulma insists on checking their ship and refuses unescorted access or a promised ride. Gohan takes both strangers only a few steps to indicate an indistinct metal edge in mist; Bulma and Goshin check the landing feet while Piccolo remains nearby. The wreck, repair, transport, departure and safe course remain unresolved.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 36 Earth water and limited consensual care
facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 36 Vegeta drinks Chi-Chi's previously offered water, declines another examination and remains guarded by Goku and Krillin. Goku proposes a later match without allowing an attack. Tien and Chiaotzu stay with Nappa while Dr. Mori, with his consent, re-dresses the scrape and listens to his breathing; he refuses a needle and transfer. No full diagnosis or settled custody follows. Vegeta retains his tail; Krillin's whole Senzu is not shown used or transferred.

facts.statement: In an independent unaccepted Chapter 36 offworld scene, a soldier, Cui and Freeza receive limited recorded fragments of the Raditz-era Chapter 6 wish discussion and the active Vegeta-scouter-era Chapter 24 exchange in which Nappa identifies a Namekian and Vegeta asks about Dragon Balls. Freeza treats another set as possible, orders a course search and asks for news of Vegeta. The two receptions are newly shown branch facts, not proof that all scouter traffic was sent or heard, that Freeza has King Kai’s private directions, that anyone on Earth or the strange world hears this scene, or that Freeza has reached Namek.

facts.statement: In unaccepted Chapter 37 Bulma and Goshin secure a loose landing-foot pin, and Gohan, Goshin and Bulma inspect the damaged wreck with Raiti and Zākuro while Piccolo guards the ship. The metal and broken systems are physically examined; Bulma cannot repair the wreck with her case or guarantee flight. Her tester detects the wreck sensor and its movements correspond in part with her ship display. This does not establish a universal mist rule, the strangers’ full powers or an invulnerable truth test.

facts.topic: chapter 37 stranded pair, assistance and promise
facts.statement: After Gohan proposes passage, Bulma refuses to put the recent would-be thieves in the cabin because of their deceptive abilities and unknown journey/supply margin. Piccolo raises the transmitter; Bulma cleans and rewires its contact and tests reception only over local distance. She warns that unknown listeners may be hostile. Zākuro decides to wait before signalling; the pair stay with the damaged wreck, two food packs, a water container and transmitter. The brothers promise to ask for help if they find someone able to come; Bulma retains route readings but cannot guarantee a return or rescue. Their true names, full abilities and future safety remain unverified.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 37 piloted exit and independent ki growth
facts.statement: Bulma chooses and pilots a route between changing markers; the ship passes the obstructed part of the current intact. From inside the ship Goshin directs ki beyond its hull to divert a broad rock and separate fragments, and Gohan independently changes another fragment’s course. Goshin’s further ordinary body-and-ki strength genuinely develops and remains afterward, alongside earlier substantial whole-hybrid growth. No numeric maximum, obligatory rate, Kaiō-ken activation, general psychic immunity, new transformation or unaided-space survival is shown.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.topic: chapter 37 Earth watch and direct call
facts.statement: Goku and Krillin watch awake Vegeta, and Tien and Chiaotzu watch Nappa. Goku adds an open rock overhang that Vegeta could leave or destroy; it does not stop an artificial moon or establish secure custody. Vegeta asks for his scouter in exchange for information; Goku refuses and actively asks about strong fighters. Chi-Chi and Goku share concern. Later Bulma connects her communicator through the ship aerial and speaks directly to Chi-Chi; the boys and Piccolo also speak, and Gohan reports two approaching presences. Chi-Chi says she will tell Goku, but that relay is not shown. Krillin’s whole Senzu is not used or transferred.
facts.source_class: authored living-character branch adaptation; not unchanged source canon or author acceptance

facts.statement: The narrator establishes that the travellers reach the same Namek reached by Freeza, but Bulma, Piccolo and the boys have not verified its name through a resident. Their ship lands intact; Bulma samples the atmosphere and receives unconfirmed radar signals, while Piccolo sees unfamiliar bright discs and the tailed boys keep their eyes down. They sense presences, contact Chi-Chi, then notice two approaching armoured scouts. Before the brothers lower ki, one scout's lens reads Gohan at 430 and Goshin at 520. Piccolo identifies scouters and the brothers lower ki without knowing those figures. At the endpoint Bulma and Piccolo are near the open hatch, Gohan and Goshin flank it, and the intact ship is behind them. No battle, ship damage, ball ownership or confirmed local sphere is shown.

facts.topic: chapter 37 independent Freeza search and approaching scouts
facts.statement: In an independent scene, Cui brings Freeza an old survey matching the recorded name Namek. Freeza reaches Namek with Zarbon and Dodoria, sees distant inhabitants and orders scouts to report people and ships; Cui is directed to seek news of Vegeta. A soldier's scouter displays unidentified settlement signals of 24, 58 and 113. Two scouts spot the travellers' vessel and begin descending; the scout who points out the ship reads Gohan at 430 and Goshin at 520 before their suppression, then asks the other to report. The other touches a scouter. These numbers are authored snapshots, not source values or maxima; receipt of the report at this chapter's endpoint, a source-mandated casualty, a ball in Freeza's possession, King Kai's private direction or shared traveller/Earth knowledge of the cutaway is not established.

facts.topic: chapter 38 scouts, suppressed and rising readings
facts.statement: Two Freeza scouts with newer-model scouters challenge the four beside their intact ship. The scout who earlier measured the boys at 430 and 520 reads suppressed Bulma 7, Piccolo 240, Gohan 310 and Goshin 360; he notices that the boys' readings have dropped. The same scout reads Gohan at 14,600 as Gohan subdues him and crushes the scouter. Goshin intercepts a hull-directed blast and directs stones away while genuine body-and-ki development occurs; the other device displays Goshin rising through 12,000 to 36,800 before Piccolo cracks it. These authored figures are snapshots, not maxima or quantified growth amounts. The scouts remain alive; their first report reaches Freeza's group and receipt of the later fighting figures is not established.

Goshin intercepts a hull-directed blast and directs stones away while genuine body-and-ki development occurs; the other device displays Goshin rising through 12,000 to 36,800 before Piccolo cracks it. The first scout reports a vessel, four occupants, a Namekian-looking person and two tails; Zarbon receives and tells Freeza. A second call breaks up; receipt of the other device’s 36,800 display is not shown. Freeza sends Zarbon and two soldiers to investigate the original landing; their arrival is not shown. Another scout reports settlement signals of 12–140; Freeza proceeds toward the settlement with Dodoria and soldiers. Bulma checks the undamaged hull and pilots the intact ship to a screened inlet.

facts.statement: Bulma directly tells Chi-Chi of scouter-wearing armoured Freeza scouts, an attempted attack and the intact ship; both sons and Piccolo speak. Chi-Chi asks Dr. Brief about transport and relays the account at the quarry. Vegeta admits serving Freeza, says Freeza is stronger, wants immortality as a chance to destroy him, warns that Freeza may seek a possible further ball set, and bargains for his ship while providing limited information about scouters and search. Goku refuses the ship. Nappa learns of Freeza's men across the tracks; Tien and Chiaotzu maintain his separate watch. facts.topic: chapter 38 Namek settlement and exact ending
facts.statement: From cover the four see green-skinned residents, children and Freeza’s soldiers at a village. An unnamed local tells Freeza he is on Namek and to leave; Piccolo hears him. Freeza asks about Dragon Balls but no resident confirms possession, rules or location, and no ball is seen. A soldier restrains an older villager and Dodoria approaches the door. Gohan moves toward the children; Goshin and Piccolo follow toward the soldier and doorway, while Bulma stays behind the ridge rock with her case. The elder turns at their approach. The intervention’s effect, any casualty, source-name identifications, ball custody and the unattended ship’s safety remain open.

Freeza associates the tailed children and Piccolo with the initial scout report and asks about the fourth. A scan of unidentified distant signals displays 210, 180 and 90. Muri infers that the devices locate people, breaks that soldier's and Dodoria's lenses and is interrupted before targeting the chair-side scouter. Goshin carries Dodoria away from the door.
